detail.abstract: This Compendium provides the integrated fiscal architecture underlying Pennsylvania's cannabis sovereignty framework and serves as the empirical backbone of the broader Keystone series. It models capital flight to neighboring jurisdictions (the "border bleed" of approximately $18 million per month, or roughly $600,000 per day), establishes an 18-month return-on-investment timeline for an in-state regulated market, and demonstrates structural insulation of the Pennsylvania General Fund from cannabis program exposure. The methodology draws on comparative state data from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, and Ohio, and applies actuarial principles to amortize transition costs across the implementation horizon. Year-by-year revenue forecasts, district-level impact disaggregation, and a defensibility analysis of all key fiscal assumptions are included. The Compendium is designed to be cited alongside the Keystone Mandate, the Keystone Doctrine, the 2026 Shafer Commission Report, and the Omnibus Amendment to Senate Bill 420, providing the underlying mathematical substrate that those documents reference but do not themselves contain. Together with the Source Compendium (citations companion, separately published), this volume completes the empirical infrastructure of the Keystone framework.

title: First and Second Price Auctions with Reselling Opportunities on Networks *

detail.title: First and Second Price Auctions with Reselling Opportunities on Networks *
detail.abstract: We study rst-price and second-price auctions in environments where bidders have opportunities to resell goods within a network, creating interdependence among bidders' valuations. While the revenue equivalence theorem establishes that, under independent private values, ecient equilibria of these two auction formats yield identical seller revenue, our model departs from this benchmark by introducing resale opportunities on social networks. We characterize the class of networks that admit ecient equilibria in the rst-price auction, which we refer to as ecient networks. Within these networks, we compare seller revenue and bidder surplus across auction formats. Our analysis demonstrates that, in ecient networks, second-price auctions generate strictly higher seller revenue than rst-price auctions. * This paper is based on Chapter 2 of my Ph.D. dissertation at Northwestern University. detail.title: Optimizing the Lean-Green Nexus: A Multi-Objective Digital Twin Architecture for Energy-Efficient Machining with Real-Time Tool Wear Compensation
detail.abstract: The transition to Industry 5.0 necessitates a shift from purely automated efficiency toward human-centric, resilient, and sustainable production orchestration. This research proposes a Multi-Objective Digital Twin architecture designed to optimize the Lean-Green-ZDM (Zero-Defect Manufacturing) nexus by synchronizing real-time physical data with a cognitive virtual core. Governed by a Cognitive-Hybrid Resilience Framework, the system integrates physics-informed power and thermal models with stochastic tool-wear estimation through a Kalman Filter to enable real-time, closed-loop parameter optimization. A dynamic Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm navigates the trade-offs between productivity, energy intensity, and surface integrity, identifying Pareto-optimal Knee Points that adapt to the tool's degradation state. Experimental validation on Ti-6Al-4V and AA7075-T6 alloys demonstrated the framework’s divergent intelligence: the MODT achieved a 62% reduction in CO2-equivalent emissions for the difficult-to-cut titanium alloy through proactive speed throttling (Resilience Mode), while simultaneously unlocking productivity headroom for the aluminum alloy (Efficiency Mode). By flattening the carbon accumulation rate and maintaining a stable Sustainable Zone, this architecture provides a robust engine for transitioning high-precision manufacturing toward a smarter, more resilient, and environmentally conscious future.

title: The Impact of Sportswashing in International Business: A Multi-Actor Framework and Research Agenda
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Impact of Sportswashing in International Business: A Multi-Actor Framework and Research Agenda
detail.abstract: This paper aims to introduce the increasingly prevalent phenomenon of ‘sportswashing’ to an international business (IB) audience. With sportswashing growing in frequency across the global sports industry, research on the subject has accelerated; however, with much of this research focused on political and ethical questions and emerging in disciplines outside IB, we argue that IB scholars are well-positioned to develop novel insights for the sportswashing literature and that this phenomenon offers new avenues for several existing streams of IB scholarship. Through an elaboration of the definitions, origin, and significance of the phenomenon, we develop a multi-actor framework for the sportswashing ecosystem, highlighting the multiple ways in which multinational enterprises (MNEs) are involved and identifying how this framework can assist IB researchers in understanding the strategic actions and incentives of the different actors. Crucially, we identify several valuable points of connection between the sportswashing phenomenon and IB, setting up an agenda for future research looking at sportswashing as a unique, hybrid form of nonmarket strategy, as well as a lens through which to explore the upgrading strategies of emerging markets and their MNEs within a global geopolitical landscape that is contested in multiple arenas – including sports.

title: Geopolitical Divergence and International Research Collaborations: Evidence from Global Firms

detail.title: Geopolitical Divergence and International Research Collaborations: Evidence from Global Firms
detail.abstract: To remain competitive in global markets, firms increasingly rely on international research collaborations (IRCs) to access diverse and critical knowledge resources. However, escalating geopolitical tensions and political divergence between nations pose growing threats to these cross-border partnerships. This study investigates how national political differences influence firms' engagement in IRCs and the boundary conditions shaping this relationship. Drawing on perspectives from political realism and techno-nationalism, we analyze secondary data from 11,160 firms across 55 countries between 2010 and 2019. Our findings reveal that political divergence significantly reduces the likelihood of IRC formation. Counterintuitively, we find that bilateral conflictual interactions weaken IRCs primarily among politically aligned nations—not among politically divergent ones—suggesting that "friendly" partnerships may be more vulnerable to geopolitical shocks. Furthermore, the negative effect of political divergence on IRCs is significantly stronger for firms in high-tech industries, reflecting the heightened role of techno-nationalist policies targeting strategically sensitive technologies. This study contributes to international management research by (1) introducing a dual-country political risk framework for understanding cross-border knowledge collaboration, (2) demonstrating that politically aligned partnerships are not immune to geopolitical disruptions, and (3) identifying high-tech firms as particularly exposed to political divergence. For managers, our findings underscore the need to incorporate geopolitical assessments into partner selection, diversify knowledge networks to mitigate over-reliance on politically aligned allies, and develop proactive strategies to safeguard access to foreign expertise in an increasingly fragmented global landscape.

title: Dispossessed in the Name of Development: Indigenous Communities and the Limits of the Right to Development

detail.title: Dispossessed in the Name of Development: Indigenous Communities and the Limits of the Right to Development
detail.abstract: The 1986 UN Declaration on the Right to Development proclaimed development as an inalienable human right belonging to every person and people. For indigenous communities, however, "development" has historically operated less as a right to be enjoyed than as a process through which existing rights are extinguished. This essay argues that the Draft Convention on the Right to Development, currently being formulated by the UN Intergovernmental Working Group, fails to adequately protect indigenous peoples from development-induced displacement. Drawing on a Third World Approaches to International Law (TWAIL) framework, and centring the experience of Adivasi communities in Wayanad, Kerala from colonial forest legislation and the 1985 Wildlife Sanctuary evictions, through the 2003 Muthanga incident and the limitations of the Forest Rights Act 2006, to the displacement following the 2024 landslides, the essay identifies three structural deficiencies in the Draft Convention: its state-centric architecture, its dilution of participation into a standard weaker than Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), and its growth-oriented framing that universalises a Western, market-based conception of development. Comparative jurisprudence from Saramaka v Suriname and the Endorois case confirms that this is a systemic global pattern. The essay concludes that without binding FPIC obligations, codified anti-displacement safeguards, and recognition of plural development models, the right to development risks becoming yet another instrument of indigenous dispossession in the name of progress.

title:
Brain Capital at the Frontier of Knowledge 
A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis of an Emerging Transdisciplinary Fields
affiliations: International University of Casablanca, Business School

detail.title:
Brain Capital at the Frontier of Knowledge 
A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis of an Emerging Transdisciplinary Fields
detail.abstract: The human brain is the most consequential — yet most systematically underinvested — asset of the modern knowledge economy. Brain Capital, defined as the aggregate stock of brain health and brain skills in individuals and populations, emerged in 2021 as a transdisciplinary framework seeking to bridge neuroscience, economics, and global public health policy. Despite explosive conceptual growth across five years and multiple extensions — including Green Brain Capital, Sleep Capital, Women’s Brain Capital, and Brain Diplomacy — no systematic mapping of this nascent literature exists. This paper addresses that gap by presenting the first systematic literature review and comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the Brain Capital field. A structured search of the Scopus database retrieved 39 records; following a rigorous two-stage pre-screening protocol combining automated keyword scoring with manual full-text assessment guided by PRISMA 2020, 10 records were excluded, yielding a validated corpus of 29 documents spanning 2021 to 2026. Nine bibliometric dimensions were examined: publication trends, document types, journal productivity, author output, keyword frequency, thematic clustering, geographic distribution, citation impact, and open access status. All 29 papers appeared within this five-year window, confirming Brain Capital as an exclusively contemporary field, with peak output in 2023–2024 and an accelerating growth trajectory. The corpus accumulated 315 Scopus citations (mean: 10.9 per paper; estimated h-index: 11), an above-average early-career impact profile for an emerging transdisciplinary field. Harris A. Eyre (n = 14 papers, 48% of the corpus) is the dominant contributor; the United States and Australia lead country-level output. Three thematic clusters are consolidating — Brain Health and Neuroscience, Economics and Policy, and Lifespan Development — while equity-focused research, standardised measurement frameworks, and Global South evidence generation remain substantially underexplored. Brain Capital is a young, rapidly accelerating, and genuinely high-impact field whose intellectual core is well-defined but narrowly concentrated. This bibliometric analysis establishes the first validated map of the Brain Capital literature and provides the field with a strategic evidence base for its next phase of development.

title: Beyond the Human Entrepreneur: Synthetic Agency, Intentionality, and the Reconceptualisation of Entrepreneurial Action in the Age of Agentic AI
affiliations: University of East London, University of East London and Ekiti State University

detail.title: Beyond the Human Entrepreneur: Synthetic Agency, Intentionality, and the Reconceptualisation of Entrepreneurial Action in the Age of Agentic AI
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurship theory rests on an unexamined premise: that the entrepreneurial actor is a biographical, embodied, morally exposed human being. Agentic artificial intelligence — systems capable of autonomous goal-setting, multi-step planning, and adaptive action — exposes this premise as a scaffold rather than a foundation. This conceptual paper interrogates four canonical pillars of entrepreneurship theory (intentionality, effectuation, opportunity creation, and judgment under uncertainty) and asks what survives, what bends, and what breaks when the actor is non-human or genuinely distributed. Drawing on the philosophy of mind and action (Davidson, Bratman, Searle, Dennett, Chalmers), we decompose entrepreneurial agency into four components — goal-directedness, means-ends reasoning, adaptive response to uncertainty, and value attribution. Engaging with functionalist critiques, we argue that agentic AI possesses the first three components but stands in a fundamentally different relation to the fourth, lacking the phenomenal stakedness — the existential "skin in the game" — that canonical theories implicitly require. From this we derive a substrate-independent typology of agency along two dimensions (source of intentionality; locus of value attribution), yielding four ideal types: the Classic Entrepreneur, the Embedded Entrepreneur, the Synthetic Agent, and the Hybrid Venture. We theorise mechanisms of movement between these cells, and we address counterarguments from human exceptionalism and the simulation/instantiation debate. Three productive tensions follow: the destabilisation of passion-based theory when intentionality is delegable; the redistribution of moral and legal responsibility when value attribution is externally assigned; and the candidacy of the entrepreneurial system as the field's new unit of analysis.

title: From Impulse to Practice: Rethinking Entrepreneurship Education through an EaP and AI Lens

detail.title: From Impulse to Practice: Rethinking Entrepreneurship Education through an EaP and AI Lens
detail.abstract: Young individuals are increasingly attracted to venture creation through social media exposure and digital entrepreneurial culture, often without the practical preparation needed for sustained venture development. Yet entrepreneurship education continues to emphasize idea generation and theory more than the everyday practices through which entrepreneurship is enacted. Drawing on Entrepreneurship as Practice (EaP), this conceptual study examines the core practices students need to learn before and during venture initiation, with particular attention to the differing demands of solo and partnership-based ventures. It argues that venture sustainability depends not only on financial resources or idea originality, but also on the consistent enactment of practices such as structured decision-making, coordination, shared responsibility, and domain-specific engagement. Furthermore, digitally mediated entrepreneurial environments expose young aspiring entrepreneurs to unverified trust-based interactions and opportunistic behavior, reinforcing the urgency of practice-based education that develops critical evaluation and verification routines. In solo ventures, decision-making is concentrated and requires strong individual preparedness, whereas partnership ventures demand active and rotating participation from all members rather than symbolic involvement. The study further explores how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can support, rather than substitute for, the development of these practices in educational settings by helping students with planning, reflection, and decision-making. By conceptualizing venture initiation and team dynamics as practice-based phenomena, this article offers a theoretically grounded foundation for entrepreneurship educators seeking to design curricula that build practical readiness for venture creation.

title: Genuine Green or Greenwashing? ESG Performance and Financial Risk Spillover in China's High-Pollution Firms
affiliations: Liaoning Technical University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Liaoning Technical University

detail.title: Genuine Green or Greenwashing? ESG Performance and Financial Risk Spillover in China's High-Pollution Firms
detail.abstract: Corporate ESG especially in heavily polluting sectors is unanimously regarded as effective way to achieve low-carbon transitions and internalize external risk. However, academic debate over whether ESG performance reflects genuine green or merely greenwashing remains, which increases the difficulty of implementing regulatory policies and the uncertainty of policy effects. Theoretically, genuine ESG instead of greenwashing can stabilize the stock price by internalizing the externality and reducing information asymmetry, therefore reducing the risk spillover. This study empirically tests whether China’s ESG performance in heavily polluting sectors is greenwashing or genuine green by investigating whether ESG performance mitigate or amplify risk spillover. We employ the LASSO-VAR model and forecast error variance decomposition (FEVD) method to construct two key risk spillover indicators—Systemic Impact and Vulnerability Degree, identify greenwashing firms, and examine the role of ESG performance on risk spillover. Empirical results show that higher overall ESG scores are associated with greater Systemic Impact and increased Vulnerability Degree, which supports the greenwashing view; further identification tests verify that greenwashing behavior significantly exacerbates systemic risk spillover. Nevertheless, the environmental pillar significantly mitigates risk spillover, whereas the social and governance pillars exacerbate it. Mechanism analysis further reveals that information asymmetry and financing constraints are the primary transmission channels underlying these effects. Our study contributes by providing micro-level evidence on the heterogeneous impacts of ESG pillars in heavily polluting industries and uncovering prevalent greenwashing behavior. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers and regulators seeking to understand the complex role of ESG in financial stability, highlighting the necessity of compulsory disclosure.

title: Toward Autonomous Cyber-Physical Production: A Multi-Stage Socio-Technical Framework for AI Integration in Machine Tool Industries

detail.title: Toward Autonomous Cyber-Physical Production: A Multi-Stage Socio-Technical Framework for AI Integration in Machine Tool Industries
detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming the machine tool industry, moving beyond isolated technological applications toward systemic integration. However, existing literature often lacks a cohesive perspective on the evolutionary process of AI adoption within manufacturing ecosystems.,This study addresses this gap by proposing a multi-stage evolutionary framework grounded in socio-technical systems theory, conceptualizing the transition from traditional craftsmanship to autonomous cyber-physical production.,The framework identifies five sequential stages of AI integration: (1) craftsmanship-based production, (2) CNC-enabled automation, (3) digital integration, (4) intelligent manufacturing, and (5) autonomous manufacturing.

title: Forecasting Türkiye’s Natural Gas Demand: A Comparative Study of Metaheuristic Algorithms Based on Meteorological and Population Indicators
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Necmettin Erbakan University

detail.title: Forecasting Türkiye’s Natural Gas Demand: A Comparative Study of Metaheuristic Algorithms Based on Meteorological and Population Indicators
detail.abstract: Accurate forecasting of natural gas demand (NGD) is critically important for nations to ensure energy security, optimize supply infrastructure, manage import dependencies, and mitigate financial risks associated with take-or-pay contracts. This study presents a novel hybrid forecasting framework that integrates demographic dynamics with multivariate meteorological data to estimate Türkiye’s natural gas demand. Unlike traditional studies in the literature that rely solely on climate-related variables such as temperature, pressure, humidity, wind, and precipitation, this study incorporates population data as an essential input parameter. Three mathematical models-linear, exponential, and quadratic-are employed, and their parameters are optimized using five different metaheuristic algorithms: artificial bee colony (ABC), differential evolution algorithm (DEA), grey wolf optimizer (GWO), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and seagull optimization algorithm (SOA). The performance of these approaches is evaluated using well-established error metrics, including mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R² ). Experiments are conducted on monthly datasets covering the period 2010-2020, with 30 independent runs for each algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating population data significantly reduces error values and improves R² across all algorithms. Among all models and algorithms, the quadratic model optimized with DEA (DEA-Q) achieves the best overall performance, with a mean R² of 0.8869 and a mean MAPE of 7.61%. The DEA and GWO algorithms exhibit superior stability with low standard deviations, while the quadratic model consistently outperforms both linear and exponential models. This study aims to provide a highly accurate forecasting framework to support energy policymakers and infrastructure planners, particularly in import-dependent countries like Türkiye.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperative Multitasking Evolutionary Algorithm for Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperative Multitasking Evolutionary Algorithm for Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization
detail.abstract: Existing constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (CMOEAs) based on evolutionarymultitasking (EMT) often suffer from the reliance on manual experience for operator selection and the adoption of static multitasking collaboration patterns, which significantly limits the search efficiency of the population. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning-driven multitask collaborative constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. A dynamic auxiliary task is created to assist the main task in solving the original constrained multi-objective optimization problem (CMOP) via knowledge transfer. This mechanism constitutes a two-task evolutionary framework. An operator pool containing three distinct search operators is established, and a hybrid action space is formulated by jointly encoding the operator selection with the multitasking collaboration patterns.The immediate reward function is designed based on the performance improvement of the main task to guide a Deep Q-Network (DQN) in learning the mapping relationship between evolutionary states and optimal actions. The trained DQN is embedded into an EMT constrained optimization framework, enabling the synergistic online adaptation of both search behavior and knowledge transfer patterns.Comparative experiments are conducted on four benchmark suites and one real-world problem, totaling 43 constrained multi-objective test functions, and the results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms seven state-of-the-art CMOEAs in terms of both convergence and diversity metrics. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the rationality and effectiveness of the key design components.

title: Equity-aware dynamic rebalancing of shared micromobility: integrating predictive prioritization with executable control
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Equity-aware dynamic rebalancing of shared micromobility: integrating predictive prioritization with executable control
detail.abstract: Shared micromobility systems can support sustainable and inclusive urban transport, yet their benefits depend on whether vehicles remain available across different areas over time. Dynamic rebalancing is challenging because demand is uneven across space and time, whereas efficiency-oriented relocation may improve average service without reducing service disparities. This study proposes an equity-aware control framework for dynamic micromobility rebalancing. The framework consists of a relocation-oriented demand prediction module (EPRFormer) and a truck-level reinforcement learning control module (EPRRL). EPRFormer predicts near-future demand pressure and identifies priority-risk zones, while EPRRL converts these signals into executable truck-level repositioning actions under operational constraints. Using Munich’s shared e-scooter system as a case study, results show that integrating predictive prioritization with executable control improves service reliability, bottom-tail protection, and shortage equity, providing a practical decision framework for balancing operational efficiency with equitable access in shared micromobility systems.

title: Overcoming the Liability of Composite Outsidership in South-South Manufacturing Investment: A Process Model of Strategic Responses
affiliations: Jinan University, Jinan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Jinan University

detail.title: Overcoming the Liability of Composite Outsidership in South-South Manufacturing Investment: A Process Model of Strategic Responses
detail.abstract: Emerging market multinationals (EMNEs) investing in other developing countries face systemic liabilities that existing theories fail to explain adequately. Through a grounded study of seven overseas factories across home appliance and new energy vehicle manufacturers, we construct a process model revealing how EMNEs overcome the liability of composite outsidership. Findings show EMNEs confront composite outsidership encompassing intertwined institutional, social, and cultural dimensions that are mutually reinforcing rather than additive. Internationalization decisions are jointly driven by a threat-opportunity simultaneity, which is translated into strategic responses through resource commitment comprising routine deployment and crisistriggered resource recursion. To overcome these multidimensional liabilities, firms develop three integrated strategies: institutional adaptation and utilization, network embeddedness-isolation, and two-way cultural integration. The process culminates in embedded autonomy, a state of deep local integration while maintaining strategic boundaries. This study extends the liability of outsidership theory to the SouthSouth context and reveals the cognitive transmission mechanism through which strategic cognition translates into action under time pressure.

title: Neutralising the free-rider effect in energy communities: A comparative analysis of benefit allocation mechanisms for balancing markets
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Valencia, Polytechnic University of Valencia and Polytechnic University of Valencia

detail.title: Neutralising the free-rider effect in energy communities: A comparative analysis of benefit allocation mechanisms for balancing markets
detail.abstract: The integration of battery energy storage systems within renewable energy communities offers a promising avenue to provide grid flexibility through balancing markets. While distributed storage is often financially unviable solely for self-consumption in small-scale residential loads, this study demonstrates that market participation significantly increases community revenues, transforming communal batteries into highly profitable investments. However, participating in bidirectional automatic frequency restoration reserve markets significantly alters local physical energy flows. We reveal that traditional revenue-sharing schemes fail to capture these economic distortions, unintentionally generating a free-rider effect where certain prosumers accrue unearned energy savings while others incur opportunity costs. To address this structural challenge, we develop a mixed-integer linear programming model to simulate an energy community's participation in automatic frequency restoration reserve markets and conduct a comparative analysis of four benefit allocation mechanisms. We propose a novel ex-post approach, the Net Opportunity Cost Allocation, which utilises a shadow settlement algorithm based on deterministic smart meter data to virtually reconstruct the pure self-consumption baseline. By structurally aligning the physical grid's impacts with financial market revenues, this method explicitly adjusts each member's market share to offset any unintended economic gains or losses. The results confirm that this mechanism completely neutralises the free-rider effect, ensuring objective financial neutrality for all participants. Ultimately, this transparent and easily implementable framework increases revenue and profitability for the energy community while ensuring that no user is penalised by market activations, thereby fostering the long-term social trust required to accelerate the widespread deployment of distributed energy resources and storage in energy communities.

detail.title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-ion Batteries Combining Impedance-based Equivalent Circuit Modeling and Data-driven Approach基于阻抗的等效电路建模与数据驱动相结合的锂离子电池健康状态估计​
detail.abstract: During lengthy service, lithium-ion batteries inevitably suffer performance decline; for this reason, a precise estimation of their state of health(SOH) becomes essential to the safe running of battery management systems. To address challenges including complex equivalent circuit model structures, difficult parameter identification, the lack of physical meaning in data-driven features, and insufficient generalization across multiple temperature conditions, this paper presents a SOH estimation method integrating electrochemical impedance modeling and deep learning. Based on the aging mechanisms of lithium-ion batteries, this work develops an improved equivalent circuit model with a streamlined structure. The model fits electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data with high accuracy, which raises the success rate of parameter identification and improves computational efficiency. Two impedance features most strongly correlated with state of health (SOH) are selected from the model parameters using Pearson correlation analysis, removing redundant information and strengthening feature interpretability. A hybrid deep network architecture that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network is then designed. This architecture extracts local spatial features from the impedance parameters and captures long-range temporal dependencies, enabling high-precision and robust SOH estimation under complex operating conditions. Experimental results show that under multiple temperature conditions, the proposed method achieves a mean absolute percentage error below 0.94%. Compared with a direct data-driven approach that does not include impedance modeling, the estimation error decreases by 20.34%, 16.47%, and 13.16% at 25°C, 35°C, and 45°C, respectively. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method features easy implementation of parameter identification, short data measurement time, high SOH estimation accuracy, and good temperature adaptability.在长时间的使用中，锂离子电池不可避免地会出现性能下降；因此，对电池健康状态（SOH）的精确估计对于电池管理系统的安全运行至关重要。为了解决等效电路模型结构复杂、参数识别困难、数据驱动特征缺乏物理意义以及在多种温度条件下泛化不足等挑战，本文提出了一种集成电化学阻抗建模和深度学习的SOH估计方法。基于锂离子电池的老化机理，本文提出了一种改进的流线型结构等效电路模型。该模型对电化学阻抗谱（EIS）数据拟合精度较高，提高了参数辨识的成功率，提高了计算效率。通过Pearson相关分析，从模型参数中选择两个与健康状态（SOH）相关性最强的阻抗特征，去除冗余信息，增强特征可解释性。然后设计了一种将卷积神经网络（CNN）与双向长短期记忆（BiLSTM）网络相结合的混合深度网络架构。该架构从阻抗参数中提取局部空间特征，并捕获长期时间依赖性，从而在复杂操作条件下实现高精度和鲁棒的SOH估计。实验结果表明，在多种温度条件下，该方法的平均绝对百分比误差在0.94%以下。与不包含阻抗建模的直接数据驱动方法相比，在25°C、35°C和45°C时，估计误差分别降低了20.34%、16.47%和13.16%。结果表明，该方法参数辨识容易实现，数据测量时间短，SOH估计精度高，具有较好的温度适应性。

title: Data Driven Approach for Fault Diagnosis of Sucker Rod Pumps: An Alternative to Manual Dynamometer Card Interpretation
affiliations: Pandit Deendayal Energy University and Pandit Deendayal Energy University

detail.title: Data Driven Approach for Fault Diagnosis of Sucker Rod Pumps: An Alternative to Manual Dynamometer Card Interpretation
detail.abstract: Sucker-rod pumps remain essential for sustaining production in mature oilfields, where real-time recognition of operational faults is critical for minimizing downtime, reducing maintenance costs, and improving production efficiency. However, conventional diagnosis of pump conditions relies heavily on manual interpretation of dynamometer cards, making the process subjective, time-intensive, and difficult to deploy consistently in field operations. Although recent advances in artificial intelligence and deep learning have improved classification performance, many existing approaches remain limited to conceptual development and lack practical integration with real-time operational workflows.This study presents a reproducible machine learning framework for automated fault diagnosis of sucker-rod pumping systems using surface dynamometer card analysis. Polished rod load–displacement signals were transformed into dynamometer cards, from which statistical, geometric, and frequency-domain features—including card area, load characteristics, stroke length, asymmetry indices, and Fourier coefficients—were extracted to characterize pump behavior. Supervised learning algorithms, including Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers, were trained to identify operational faults such as incomplete fillage, gas interference, and rod parting. Systematic Minority Oversampling was applied to address class imbalance associated with infrequent events such as pump hitting. The proposed workflow was validated through cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization, achieving an overall accuracy of 97%, with precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.97. The framework demonstrates the feasibility of integrating data-driven diagnostics with real-time field operations, bridging conventional dynamometer card interpretation and intelligent artificial lift monitoring for improved operational transparency and decision support.

detail.abstract: This note arose from an inheritance-tax design problem (Cornell 2026) that required a benchmark for returns on investments that an executor could compute and a tax auditor could verify. The standard candidates from academic finance (Jensen 1968, Fama-French 1993, 2015, Carhart 1997) are model-dependent residuals not suited to that purpose. What is usable is the realized total return on a low-cost broad-market index fund, and it turned out to be the same quantity Bogle, Malkiel, Sharpe, Ellis, and Buffett have been measuring for fifty years without using a standardized vocabulary. We define practical alpha as α p = r-r V , where r is the realized return on the investor's portfolio and r V is the realized total return on a low-cost total market index fund (e.g., Vanguard's VTI). The contribution is terminological, not theoretical. Retail investor discourse lacks a stable, easy-to-use vocabulary distinguishing benchmark-relative realized outperformance (what investors want) from model-relative residual outperformance (what the academic literature measures). Academic alphas do not compete with α p ; they stand in a precise mathematical relationship to it as decompositions under various factor models. Both are correct for their domains; they simply answer different questions. Naming the quantity that practical investors really care about makes the relationship visible and the popular-finance literature easier to read.

title: Consolidated-Standalone Revenue Gap and Capital Market Mispricing: Evidence from Korean Dual-Reporting Firms

detail.title: Consolidated-Standalone Revenue Gap and Capital Market Mispricing: Evidence from Korean Dual-Reporting Firms
detail.abstract: Korea’s mandatory simultaneous disclosure of standalone and consolidated financial statements creates a mechanically computable measure of intra-group revenue flows: the Consolidated-Standalone Revenue Gap (CSRG), defined as standalone minus consolidated sales scaled by lagged total assets. Using 25,541 firm-year observations for KOSPI/KOSDAQ non-financial firms from 2012 to 2023, I document three findings. First, CSRG is negatively associated with one-year-ahead consolidated ROA (−0.006, p < 0.10 full sample; −7.43, p < 0.05 in the CSRG > 0 subsample, N = 596), consistent with intra-group standalone revenue behaving as a low-reliability accrual that reverses at consolidation. CSRG is empirically orthogonal to Modified Jones discretionary accruals (Pearson ρ = 0.001) and retains incremental predictive content when entered jointly with established earnings-quality measures (Dechow et al. 1995; Kothari et al. 2005; Dechow and Dichev 2002). Second, the level of CSRG is positively associated with one-year cumulative abnormal returns (+0.033, p < 0.01); a persistent–transitory decomposition shows the return association is driven entirely by the persistent component (β = +0.058, p < 0.01), evidence that the market prices structural intra-group activity. Third—and most novel—the year-over-year change in CSRG (ΔCSRG) predicts abnormal returns with the opposite sign from the level (CSRG_W = +0.042; ΔCSRG_W = −0.100; both p < 0.01), replicating in buy-and-hold returns and revealing that the market underreacts to transitory accelerations in intra-group revenue recognition. Foreign institutional ownership attenuates this mispricing (CSRG × INST_LOG: β = −30.5, p < 0.01), and the moderation result is robust across nine specifications. The findings introduce a directly observable consolidation-based earnings-reliability signal that complements model-estimated discretionary accruals and informs auditor risk assessment and regulatory monitoring of intra-group transactions.

title: Bridging the Green Divide: How Green Technological Innovation and Natural Resources Endowment Drive Emissions Across Economies

detail.title: Bridging the Green Divide: How Green Technological Innovation and Natural Resources Endowment Drive Emissions Across Economies
detail.abstract: This study examines how green technological innovation (GI), natural resource endowment (NTRS), and some other key factors drive sectoral and aggregate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across developed and emerging markets. In doing this, we employed the Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS), and we found significant variations in the effects of drivers across emerging and developed economies. For instance, in emerging markets, we found that an increase in aggregate economic activities and industrial output upsurges GHG emissions while growth in agricultural output reduces it. However, in developed economies, an increase in economic activities and agricultural output is decoupled from GHG emissions, while industrial output negatively and significantly impacts it. Furthermore, we found that GI reduces sectoral GHG emissions across all economies and aggregate GHG emissions in emerging markets. Still, we discovered a rebound effect on aggregate GHG emissions in developed economies. Additionally, we found variations in the sectoral and aggregate effect of NTRS and other prominent drivers on GHG emissions across economies. Our findings carry substantial policy implications.

detail.title: Governing the Inclusive Insurance Commons
detail.abstract: We argue that an insurance risk pool is a common-pool resource subject to the "tragedy of the commons." Applying Ostrom's (1990) eight design principles to insurance, we show that each implies governance requirements formalisable using established results from risk sharing and capital allocation theory. This yields a diagnostic checklist of eight axioms organised along three dimensions of inclusive insurance: availability, affordability, and accessibility. The checklist identifies both what is failing in an inclusive insurance scheme and why, pointing to the required governance intervention. Applications to mutual health organisations, index-based livestock insurance, and peer-to-peer platforms demonstrate the framework's value.

detail.abstract:
Background: ​Hysterectomy is one of the most frequent gynaecological procedures worldwide, yet its patterns remain poorly characterised in many middle-income countries. We aimed to describe trends, geographic variation, surgical routes, technicity indices, and their association with human development indices of hysterectomy in Brazil from 2008 to 2024. 

Methods: We conducted a nationwide, population-based, ecological time-series study using data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). All hysterectomies performed for non-malignant conditions between January 2008 and December 2024 were included. Age-standardised rates were calculated for each state and year. The technicity index (proportion of minimally invasive procedures) and patient travel distances were quantified. Correlations with the Human Development Index (HDI) were assessed using Spearman’s coefficient. Temporal trends were modelled with linear mixed-effects models and non-parametric sensitivity analyses. 

Findings: Among 1,550,552 hysterectomies for non-malignant conditions, the early mortality rate was 1·1 per 1000. The national age-standardised rate was 116·1 per 100,000 women, remaining stable during the pre-pandemic period (β = −0·29 per year; 95% CI: −1·88 to 1·29; p = 0·717). We identified a clear seasonal pattern peaking in October (+14·1%). Minimally invasive techniques were used in only 7·9% of procedures in 2024, and the mean technicity index was low across all states (9·5 ± 5·3). States with lower HDI exhibited significantly higher hysterectomy rates (Spearman's rho ≈ −0·46) and even lower technicity indices (ρ = −0·53). Patients in the Central-West and North regions travelled more than 170 km on average. Interstate variability is high and increased following the COVID-19 pandemic. 

Interpretation: In contrast to high-income nations, Brazil exhibited no significant reduction in hysterectomy rates but revealed low adoption of minimally invasive techniques nationwide and profound subnational inequalities. Higher procedure rates and even lower technicity indices were consistently observed in less developed states. These findings underscore that hysterectomy practices reflect deeper structural inequities within the healthcare system. Funding None.

title: Beyond Rignano: The Benchmark Question in Generational Inheritance Taxation

detail.abstract: Jefferson’s desire to avoid an aristocracy of wealth is why inheritance taxes have long been favored. Proposals descending from Rignano (1901, 1919) address dynastic wealth by increasing the tax on transfers as generations increase from the founders; recent design work by Halliday (2018) and Fleischer (2020, 2024) has refined the implementation, with Fleischer proposing an imputed risk-free rate of return as the relevant baseline for distinguishing inherited from created wealth. This paper argues that the entire Rignano tradition has been working in the wrong frame. Once compounding at the systemic real return—what Buffett calls the American Tailwind—is taken as the central variable, the design problem is not how to refine generation-counting or how to set rates within Rignano’s framework; it is how to choose a benchmark that absorbs the tailwind. We show that under Fleischer’s specified design, applied to a passively indexed dynasty at replacement fertility, per-capita wealth grows by approximately a factor of 2.7 per generation; across three generations the per-capita growth factor approaches 19. We introduce a biological dilution test as the operational form of Jefferson’s structural objective and prove a threshold result: any benchmark close to the systemic return on the productive economy passes the test, and any benchmark at or near the risk-free rate fails. When the benchmark line is drawn exempting the equity premium as “first-generation wealth,” it hands heirs the return that comes from being born into a productive economy. The class of tailwind-aware regimes that pass the test is in principle broader than a single design, but alternatives to a direct market-return benchmark add estimation choices and administrative complexity that the simpler design avoids. The Generational Benchmark Inheritance Regime developed in companion work, which sets its benchmark at the total market return itself, is the obvious tailwind-aware regime and the only design currently in the inheritance-tax literature whose benchmark sits in the range that satisfies the structural objective. What is needed is not a modified Rignano. What is needed is a tailwind-aware regime.

title: Automation, Purchasing Power, and Systemic Imbalance: A Universal Balance-Feedback Framework Analysis of Advanced Capitalism

detail.title: Automation, Purchasing Power, and Systemic Imbalance: A Universal Balance-Feedback Framework Analysis of Advanced Capitalism
detail.abstract: Advanced capitalism faces a deep structural contradiction when automation displaces labor at scale: the very mechanism that maximizes productive efficiency also destroys the mass purchasing power upon which demand-driven economies depend. This paper formalizes this contradiction within the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF), operationalizing its Four Universal Laws-System Integrity, Universal Balance, Feedback Loop Mechanism, and Interconnected Nodes-as a coupled dynamical system governing the co-evolution of automation, wages, purchasing power, and ownership concentration. We derive conditions for systemic equilibrium and disequilibrium, conduct Lyapunov stability analysis on four future scenarios (hyper-oligarchy, Universal Basic Income, post-scarcity hybrid, and systemic collapse), and identify ownership structure as the master bifurcation variable. We further situate the analysis within existing literature on labor-displacement, financialization as a temporary demand buffer, and historical precedent from prior technological transitions. We conclude that the central economic question of advanced civilization shifts from production adequacy to access distribution, and that the UBFF provides a unifying formal architecture for modeling this transition.

detail.title: Robust Likelihood-Based Regression for Differential Expression and Splicing Using Normal-Power Transformation Models
detail.abstract: Transcriptomic data at high throughputs are known to have long-term non-conformity to the classical regression conditions, such as heavy-tailed residues, dependence of mean on variance and bound values like percent-spliced-in (PSI) values. Differential expression and splicing analysis are standard tools used in the analysis of differential expression and splicing, such as negative binomial and beta regression models. They assume restrictive distributional models, which can cause the inference to be unstable in the presence of extreme observations or non-homogenous noise. In the current research, a strong likelihood-based regression model is presented, which adopted the Normal-Power (N-P) transformation framework. It incorporates a Gaussian baseline in a power-function tail to fit skewness, heavy tails and restricted support into a single formulation. The method achieves interpretability of regression effects, and makes full-likelihood inference of both regression measures of abundance (continuous), and unit-bounded splicing phenotypes. It was estimated through profiled maximum likelihood using closed-form inner updates making it genome-wide scalable. The research illustrate an objective recovery of parameters, a rational Wald coverage and stable convergence using different tail values and sample sizes through simulation studies. RNA-seq and splicing were applied on the data, Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohort of lung adenocarcinoma applications, which reveal that the N-P model has better goodness-of-fit, well-calibrated p-values and discoveries that are reproducible over competing models, and has controlled false discovery rates. Adequacy of the models is also further evidenced by diagnostics using probability integral transforms and residual behaviour. The suggested framework offers an alternative approach to the analysis of heavy-tailed and bounded biomedical data that is statistically principled and computationally efficient, gives continuous models that lie between the Gaussian, log-normal and bounded-response models and is a likelihood-based model that is now applicable in modern medical genomics.

detail.abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) has, on the one hand, made daily computing activities efficient and effortless, and at the same time created public anxieties over employment. Such apprehension is further reinforced by fluctuations in the labor market, as confirmed by several public surveys, creating uncertainties in both the labor market and the political sphere. This policy brief evaluates the current macroeconomic knowledge of AI, especially its effects on jobs and growth. The analysis suggests that AI's impact will disproportionately affect different sectors of the economy. Moreover, AI is likely to shift the demand curve for skills, making it imperative for workers to prepare for an uncertain future in which existing skills may not be sufficient. AI-related investment has contributed 0.9% to real GDP growth of the U.S. in 2025, but long-term labor-market resilience depends on balancing innovation with job creation (Rubinton and Patro 2026). Sustained economic progress will also require policymakers to focus on infrastructure investment, workforce retraining, and AI literacy to ensure that AI strengthens rather than destabilizes the broader economy.

detail.abstract: Dealer gamma exposure governs how market makers hedge, and that hedging creates distinct intraday price dynamics. When dealers are long gamma, their hedging suppresses index moves; when short, it amplifies them. This paper exploits that causal structure. A three-state Hidden Markov Model fitted to dealer gamma exposure classifies each trading day into one of three microstructure regimes: Pin (stabilizing), Vacuum (neutral), or Accelerant (destabilizing). A structured transition prior enforces the physical constraint that the index cannot jump directly between polar regimes-all transitions pass through a neutral gateway. Within each regime, direction is predicted by gradient-boosted models whose architecture adapts to the regime: squared-error regression for trending markets, absolute-error regression for outlier-heavy environments, and binary classification for compression regimes where the question is direction, not magnitude. Entry quality is filtered through conviction gates discovered independently from the predictive model using a two-phase methodology: first, identify microstructure conditions that predict directional outcomes across the full regime population; second, apply those conditions to model-generated signals. This separation prevents the gates from overfitting to the model's specific trade selections. Post-entry, dealer flow monitoring closes positions when the supporting microstructure begins to erode, lifting win rates by 12 percentage points. Over a 15-month walk-forward out-of-sample period (January 2025 through March 2026), the framework produces 321 trades across six directional sleeves with a 77% win rate (z = 9.54, p = 1.1 × 10-22) and +3,063 realized S&P 500 points. Every quarterly fold is profitable. Randomizing regime labels collapses performance to coin-flip levels, confirming that the regime conditioning carries genuine signal. The directional predictions are instrument-agnostic and can be expressed through same-day options, index futures, or leveraged ETFs depending on the practitioner's risk profile.

title: Urban Development Parameter Reset: An Operational Manual — A Behavioral Dynamics-Based Governance Toolkit for Catch-Up Cities

detail.title: Urban Development Parameter Reset: An Operational Manual — A Behavioral Dynamics-Based Governance Toolkit for Catch-Up Cities
detail.abstract: This manual translates the four-parameter diagnostic framework developed in the companion theoretical paper From Drift to Lock-In: A Behavioral Parameter Mechanism of Urban Development into an actionable toolkit for prefectural-level city mayors and their policy research offices. It addresses a practical question that follows from the theoretical diagnosis: once a city recognizes that its development parameters are suspended, what concrete steps can a mayor take within their term and authority to reset them? The manual provides a 12-item self-assessment scale (three items each for Goal Clarity, Stakeholder Resonance, Identity Commitment, and Agency Threshold), a two-tier trigger mechanism distinguishing municipal self-rescue from provincial-level support, and four sets of reset levers-ranging from institutionalizing a city positioning white paper to launching a reverse due diligence on target industries, from building an industrial landmark to establishing a trial-and-error fund and a mayor-sponsored critical project. A post-reset verification checklist and a diagnostic quick-reference card are also included. All tools are designed to be initiated within the mayor's existing authority and to yield observable results within one planning cycle. The manual also records publicly verifiable facts from two historical cases-Kunshan's self-funded development zone (1984) and Hefei's investment in BOE (2008)-as references for how Agency Threshold can be activated during institutional windows before full policy authorization is in place. The manual concludes with the mechanism through which the four parameter resets create conditions for the triple lock-in (asset, interest, and brand) identified in the theoretical paper, thereby transforming cadre rotation from a trigger of parameter drift into a driver of parameter consolidation.

title: Arj Samarakoon and the Reform Imperative: A Policy Framework for Expanding Foreign Direct Investment in Sri Lanka

detail.title: Arj Samarakoon and the Reform Imperative: A Policy Framework for Expanding Foreign Direct Investment in Sri Lanka
detail.abstract: Sri Lanka's economic recovery offers a narrow window to convert macroeconomic stability into sustained foreign direct investment (FDI). Drawing on reform principles advanced by Arj Samarakoon (2025) and comparative evidence from emerging markets, this paper outlines a policy framework to scale annual FDI inflows from under one billion United States dollars to a multi-billion trajectory. The proposed framework emphasises regulatory predictability, empowered facilitation, prepared project pipelines, and diaspora co-investment. Using data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF, 2024), the World Bank (2024), and the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI, 2024), the paper develops a twelve-month reform roadmap designed to improve investor confidence and signal credibility to global capital markets.

title: Arjuna Samarakoon on Informal Economies, Participation, and the Structural Limits of Emerging Markets

detail.title: Arjuna Samarakoon on Informal Economies, Participation, and the Structural Limits of Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: The informal economy is frequently discussed as a structural weakness within developing countries, yet it also represents a form of adaptive participation that emerges when formal systems become inaccessible, inefficient, or insufficiently responsive. This paper examines the informal economy not merely as an issue of regulation or tax compliance, but as a reflection of how individuals navigate economic systems under constraint. Drawing on the systems-oriented public thinking associated with Arjuna Samarakoon, the discussion explores the relationship between accessibility, trust, participation, and economic adaptation. Rather than viewing informal activity solely as an economic problem, the paper argues that it should also be understood as a signal indicating where formal systems fail to absorb participation effectively. For Sri Lanka, long-term economic inclusion depends not only on reducing informality, but on designing formal systems that are efficient, understandable, and economically meaningful to ordinary participants.

title: Institutional Resilience and Economic Recovery Models: A Public Commentary Featuring Arjuna Samarakoon

detail.title: Institutional Resilience and Economic Recovery Models: A Public Commentary Featuring Arjuna Samarakoon
detail.abstract: Institutional trust is increasingly recognized as a foundational condition for economic stability, investment confidence, and long-term development. While economic discussions often focus on fiscal policy, infrastructure, and market performance, the credibility of institutions quietly shapes how individuals and businesses respond to those conditions. This paper examines the relationship between institutional trust and economic behavior in emerging economies, particularly during periods of uncertainty and structural adjustment. Drawing on the systemsoriented public commentary associated with Arjuna Samarakoon, the discussion argues that trust should not be treated merely as a governance issue, but as an economic variable with direct consequences for participation, investment, and productivity. Countries with higher levels of institutional credibility tend to experience stronger economic coordination, lower friction, and more stable participation. For Sri Lanka, the challenge is not only improving institutions operationally, but rebuilding confidence in how those institutions function and communicate.

title:
A Micro-Equation for Economic Action:
Action Generation under Path-Absence

detail.title:
A Micro-Equation for Economic Action:
Action Generation under Path-Absence
detail.abstract:
Existing theories often implicitly presuppose that choice becomes action. This paper explicitly formalizes that missing link: how an economic action is generated when no path is given ex ante. From three axioms and the structural properties of the probability function, we derive the direction coefficient k and obtain the action equation

  dx = k · s · w · dφ,

where dφ is the local expected surplus, s is loss–gain sensitivity, w is probability weighting, and k is determined by the optimal input intensity. This equation specifies both direction and intensity from local information alone, without presupposing an ex ante path or transition rule. We further show that classical optimality conditions — the equimarginal principle, P = MC, and NPV = 0 — can be interpreted as boundary conditions where the action incentive is exhausted (dφ = 0). This paper provides a minimal structure for action generation that serves as a common micro-framework for diverse economic actions.

title: Preparing for Liftoff: Privatization Alternatives for Canada's Airports

detail.title: Preparing for Liftoff: Privatization Alternatives for Canada's Airports
detail.abstract: The cost performance of Canada’s airports has fallen under scrutiny in recent years as airports represent one of the few major revenue-generating assets wholly owned by the federal government of Canada that could potentially be tapped for funds. Most recently, in November 2025, Prime Minister Mark Carney and his government appeared to suggest in the fall budget that a proposed $25 billion sovereign wealth fund could be funded in part by privatization of Canada’s airports. This would go beyond existing initiatives to allow airports to partner with private companies via co-development through subleases, subcontracting airport services and investment through airport authority subsidiaries. However, even though full privatization has long been implemented by countries like the UK, this article argues that it is not advisable from the political and economic perspectives for Canada to sell off all eight major airports to the private sector. Instead, the government should consider the mixed ownership models from successful airports in Asia to ensure that privatization can both raise much-needed funds while improving airport infrastructure, efficiency, and cost performance.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Book: Behavioral Economics: Institutional Engineering for the AI Age

detail.abstract: The digital platforms that now mediate a substantial share of social and economic life present institutional theory with a defining paradox. On the one hand, platforms produce behavioral trace data of a granularity and scale unimaginable in the era of classical institutionalism-billions of timestamped reactions to informational signals. On the other hand, the foundational definitions of the discipline, particularly those inherited from Douglass North and W. Richard Scott, fail to travel to this data in any operationally coherent way. Drawing on a systematic review of the A/B testing architectures of Meta and Google, this study demonstrates that the conceptual apparatus of institutions-as-rules is not merely difficult to operationalize but is structurally incompatible with how real behavioral patterns emerge, stabilize, and dissolve on digital platforms. The paper documents three empirical fracture points: the algorithmic disruption of random assignment in platform experiments, the systematic exclusion of demographic groups from informational signals via opaque machine-learning optimization, and the platform-as-institutional-environment problem, wherein the signal generator itself is the primary architect of behavioral spectra. Anchored in Rapoport's subjectivism of system-identification, we propose that institutions must be reconceived as empirically distinguishable, statistically stable clusters of behavioral trajectories-carved from data by the analyst, not discovered as pre-existing entities. This redefinition provides the conceptual foundation for a full three-tier research program encompassing base definitions, a theoretical explanatory scaffold, and a suite of mathematical operationalization tools.

title: SIGoT® (Integrated Territorial Governance System): A Methodological Framework for Ex Ante Territorial Coherence and Decision Structuring

detail.title: SIGoT® (Integrated Territorial Governance System): A Methodological Framework for Ex Ante Territorial Coherence and Decision Structuring

keywords.keywords: Territorial Governance Ex Ante Decision-Making Territorial Coherence Identity-Based Planning Rural Governance Environmental Governance Spatial Planning Governance Framework Territorial Identity Decision Theory Epistemology of Territory Multi-Level Governance Risk Governance Landscape Governance Systemic Planning

contentFormat.other: Methodological and epistemological framework for territorial governance

detail.abstract:
SIGoT® (Sistema Integrato di Governo del Territorio) is an original methodological and systemic framework designed to address one of the main structural weaknesses of contemporary territorial governance: the growing asymmetry between the increasing availability of territorial data and the declining capacity to produce coherent, governable and defensible territorial decisions.

The framework introduces an epistemological shift from analytical fragmentation toward identity-based territorial interpretation. Instead of treating territory as a mere aggregation of datasets, constraints, GIS layers or sectoral analyses, SIGoT® conceptualizes territory as a structured identity system composed of permanences, recurrences, fragilities, dynamics and territorial prevalences.

The methodological architecture is based on a mandatory sequential structure articulated in four interconnected phases: identity reading, decision structuring, coherence verification and output generation. Within this structure, territorial coherence is not treated as a technical compliance check but as an ex ante epistemological boundary defining the governability of transformations before project formalization.

A central theoretical contribution of the framework is the introduction of the concept of “ungoverned risk”, defined as the risk generated by territorial decisions adopted without prior identity interpretation, alternative evaluation, reversibility assessment and structural coherence verification.

SIGoT® does not propose a software system, GIS platform or administrative procedure. It is conceived as a modular and scalable governance framework aimed at supporting territorial decision-making, reducing discretionary fragmentation, improving institutional defensibility and strengthening ex ante governance capacity in territorial, rural and environmental policies.

The work positions itself as a conceptual and methodological contribution to contemporary territorial governance theory, with potential applications in planning systems, environmental governance, rural policy, landscape governance and multi-level institutional decision processes.

title: Informal Economies, Trust Deficits, and the Cost of Institutional Delay in South Asia: A Commentary Linked to the Public Systems Thinking of Arjuna Samarakoon

detail.title: Informal Economies, Trust Deficits, and the Cost of Institutional Delay in South Asia: A Commentary Linked to the Public Systems Thinking of Arjuna Samarakoon
detail.abstract: Economic productivity is commonly measured through labour output, capital investment, infrastructure development, and industrial performance. However, one of the most overlooked constraints in emerging economies is the economic cost of time lost through inefficiency, administrative delays, and institutional friction. This paper examines how waiting costs and procedural inefficiencies quietly reduce productivity across households, businesses, and public systems. Drawing on the systems-oriented public thinking associated with Arjuna Samarakoon, the discussion argues that time should be treated as an economic resource rather than merely a scheduling issue. Economies that reduce friction often improve participation, increase investment confidence, and strengthen institutional trust without necessarily increasing expenditure. For Sri Lanka, improving productivity may depend less on producing more and more on reducing the hidden losses created by inefficient systems.

title: TIMEFRAME STATE CROSSOVER SIGNALS IN THE MELGO SEQUENCE FRAMEWORK: Directional Accuracy at the Alignment Event Across Four Asset Classes — State-Disaggregated Analysis

detail.title: TIMEFRAME STATE CROSSOVER SIGNALS IN THE MELGO SEQUENCE FRAMEWORK: Directional Accuracy at the Alignment Event Across Four Asset Classes — State-Disaggregated Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was conducted independently with no institutional affiliation, funding, or financial relationship that could be perceived to have influenced the study. The author has no conflicts of interest to declare.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a directional asymmetry finding in the Melgo Sequence framework — a price structure classification system built on the behavioral properties of HL2, HLC3, and OHLC4 as structural market levels. When a faster timeframe structural state aligns to match a slower timeframe state (a crossover event), the next 4H candle follows the predicted direction 67–83% of the time across four instruments (all p<0.001). When the slower timeframe aligns to the faster, results are statistically indistinguishable from chance (0 of 4 cells significant, all p>0.10).

State-disaggregated analysis of faster-to-4H crossovers (n=1,718–2,605 per instrument across BTCUSDT, SPY, EURUSD, and NASDAQ) reveals that the aggregate accuracy figure conceals strongly differentiated state-level effects. Three states — Bull Trend, Bear Trend, and Bull Rejection — produce 86–94% directional accuracy at crossover, all p<0.001. Bear Indecision produces 62–74% bearish resolution at crossover, all p<0.01. Distribution produces 61–64% bullish accuracy at crossover — inverting the framework's single-timeframe bearish label. Accumulation produces approximately 91% bearish accuracy at crossover on BTC, SPY, and NASDAQ — a complete inversion of the bullish framework label — documented in full in the companion paper (Melgo, 2026c, The Accumulation Paradox).

The state-disaggregated findings are the primary new contribution of this study. They establish that crossover direction alone is not the signal — the specific state shared at the moment of alignment determines both the direction and the magnitude of the predictive effect. A previously reported 95.2% accuracy figure for the 4H→1H EURUSD pair is corrected to 49.4%, a null result arising from a script artifact identified and resolved in this study.

This is the second paper in the Melgo Sequence research series. The primary paper (Melgo, 2026a) is submitted to Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities. Pine Script backtesting scripts are available upon request at @JeffMelgo on TradingView.

title: Administrative Interconnectivity and the Failure of Social Justice: A Multi-Agency Case Study of Agrarian Rights in the Philippines

detail.title: Administrative Interconnectivity and the Failure of Social Justice: A Multi-Agency Case Study of Agrarian Rights in the Philippines
detail.abstract: Agrarian reform is often analysed as a bilateral conflict between the State and a landowner. This paper argues that the success of land emancipation is actually contingent upon a complex "administrative ecosystem." Using the case of CA-G.R. SP No. 89360 (Victoria P. Cabral vs. Heirs of Felipe Angeles), this study examines how the nullification of land titles due to a Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) procedural error triggers a "domino effect" of rights violations involving local Barangay governance, law enforcement (PNP), and public utilities (Meralco). The paper establishes that the heirs occupy a state of "Administrative Suspension," where technical title cancellation is weaponized to deny basic human rights, despite the survival of Vested Agrarian Rights. title: The Accumulation Paradox: State-Specific Directional Inversion at Crossover Events in the Melgo Sequence Framework

detail.title: The Accumulation Paradox: State-Specific Directional Inversion at Crossover Events in the Melgo Sequence Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was conducted independently with no institutional affiliation, funding, or financial relationship that could be perceived to have influenced the study. The author has no conflicts of interest to declare.

detail.abstract:
This paper documents the Accumulation Paradox: in the Melgo Sequence framework, the crossover alignment event — where a faster timeframe (15m or 1H) transitions into the same Accumulation state as the slower 4H timeframe — produces bearish directional accuracy of approximately 90% across four structurally diverse instruments (BTCUSDT, SPY, EURUSD, NASDAQ), all p<0.001. The Melgo Sequence classifies Accumulation as a bullish structural state at the single-timeframe level, where it produces 62.3% bullish accuracy on BTCUSDT (p=0.0021, n=162). The crossover event inverts that label entirely.

The inversion is consistent across all four instruments and across three consecutive 4H candles (N+1, N+2, N+3). At N+1, bearish accuracy is 89.3–90.4% with Wilson 95% CIs of [80–95%]. At N+3 — 12 hours of 4H price action after the event — bearish accuracy remains 69.1–75.9%, CIs remaining above 61% on all instruments. Twelve independent statistical cells (four instruments × three windows), all p<0.001, eliminate the possibility of a timing artifact. An independent verification script built from scratch confirms the finding is genuine. A Bull Trend crossover control group produces a structurally symmetric bullish persistence trajectory, confirming script integrity.

We introduce the Exhaustion Hypothesis as a post-hoc mechanistic interpretation: when the faster timeframe enters Accumulation to match the 4H, the compressive structure may be at maximum extent across timeframe levels, marking completion rather than continuation of the accumulation phase. This hypothesis is one of several possible explanations consistent with the data and has not been independently tested.

This finding establishes a critical distinction for the framework: a structural state's directional meaning depends on the temporal context of observation. As a static completed-candle reading, Accumulation is bullish. As a dynamic crossover alignment event, Accumulation is the strongest bearish signal in the framework.

This is the third paper in the Melgo Sequence research series. The primary framework paper (Melgo, 2026a) and the crossover directional asymmetry study (Melgo, 2026b) are available as SSRN preprints. Pine Script verification scripts are available upon request at @JeffMelgo on TradingView.
