title: When the Headquarters Becomes a Branch

detail.title: When the Headquarters Becomes a Branch

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict

detail.abstract: This paper studies how bank mergers change local credit production when a target headquarters becomes a branch. Acquired-bank production falls sharply and persistently in the former-headquarters county, conditional on the survivor's pre-merger local platform. Observable terms do not deteriorate, and replacement appears at incumbent local banks and thrifts rather than independent nonbank lenders. The pattern reflects reassignment of a headquarters-centered production franchise: losses concentrate when buyer and target headquarters lie in different local banking markets, are muted within the same market, and are larger where the target had a deeper pre-merger branch network. The organizational geography of bank consolidation reshapes local credit portfolios while aggregate supply is preserved.

title: The Robber Barons of Beijing: Can China Survive Its Gilded Age?

detail.title: The Robber Barons of Beijing: Can China Survive Its Gilded Age?
detail.abstract: Yuen Yuen Ang argues that China’s sustained growth alongside rampant corruption is not a paradox, but a result of a specific variety of graft: access money. By disaggregating corruption into distinct types, Ang shows that while petty theft and speed money hinder growth, access money—high-stakes exchanges for exclusive privileges—functions like "steroids," fueling rapid infrastructure development while nesting systemic financial risks. This system emerged from Deng Xiaoping’s "directed improvisation," which incentivized local officials to act as surrogate entrepreneurs. However, Ang contends that Xi Jinping’s top-down anticorruption campaign, while effective at instilling fear, fails to address the state's outsized economic power and has inadvertently suppressed the bottom-up experimentation essential for long-term adaptability. She concludes that sustainable reform requires a structural shift away from command-and-control governance toward fundamental fiscal and institutional changes.

title: How Washington Ended a War on Paper Operation Epic Fury, the War Powers Resolution, and the Erosion of Congressional War Authority

detail.title: How Washington Ended a War on Paper Operation Epic Fury, the War Powers Resolution, and the Erosion of Congressional War Authority
detail.abstract: On May 1, 2026, the sixty-day clock set by the War Powers Resolution of 1973 expired on Operation Epic Fury-the U.S. air campaign against Iran-without a congressional vote authorizing its continuation. Rather than seeking authorization or withdrawing forces, the Trump administration sent a letter to congressional leadership declaring hostilities concluded on the executive's own authority, while simultaneously preserving the full military posture, threat framework, and option to resume strikes. This paper analyses the constitutional, institutional, and strategic implications of that manoeuvre. It argues that the administration's letter does not merely circumvent the War Powers Resolution-it establishes a new precedent: an executive that can declare a war ended on paper while retaining every instrument of war in theatre, and a Congress that, given eight opportunities to assert its constitutional authority, declined each one. The paper traces the anatomy of the legal off-ramp, situates Epic Fury within the longer history of presidential war-making from Korea to Syria, and examines what the parallel erosion of civilian military oversight-through the firing of senior officers by Defense Secretary Hegseth-reveals about the structural direction of American civil-military relations. It concludes that the constitutional balance Madison designed to be self-enforcing through competing ambitions has, in practice, produced a system in which the executive writes its own exits and Congress gratefully takes them.

title: Persistency of Climatic/Hydrological Drought Effect on the Ubangi River Regime at Bangui, Central African Republic

detail.title: Persistency of Climatic/Hydrological Drought Effect on the Ubangi River Regime at Bangui, Central African Republic
detail.abstract: This article discusses/assesses the persistent effect of climatic/hydrological drought on the Ubangi River regime at Bangui over the 1935-2025 period, dividing in dry period (1971-2025), and wet to wettest one (1935-1970). The analysis was based on the annual regimes of discharge and volume mobilized by the basin aquifer on different time scales.The SDI index shows a drought’s moderate impact on flow, and on the coupled evolution of depletion coefficient-basin’s mobilized volume per aquifer between wet and dry periods. Since 1971, depletion is predominant (0.0169 day-1 in 1935-1961, 0.0189 day-1 in 1962-1990, and 0.0209 day-1 in 1991-2021), while the aquifer’ volume mobilized decreases steadily (53 km3 in 1935-1966, 43 km3 in 1967-1981, and 34 km3 in 1982-2021). The annual discharge-volume mobilized per aquifer, and volume mobilized-depletion coefficient correlations are strong, respectively R: 0.71 and 0.82, compared with the annual discharge-depletion coefficient relation (R = 0.54).Drought impact on the fluvial regime was weak in the 1970s, and severe since 1981. Groundwater was also well affected in 1984, 1990, 1993, 2000, and 2018, and particularly over the 2005-2013 period (32 km3 in average), compared to the length one 1971-2023 (35 km3 on average). Thus, progressive and accentuated deficits are identified in both discharge (-0.2% in 1970-1980, and -19% in 1981-2023), and basin’s volume mobilized per aquifer (-21% in 1982-2023), while the depletion coefficient increased (+11% in 1991-2023). These results attest to the persistent impact of the current drought accentuation on the Ubangi flow at Bangui, mainly in 1980/1990, as water resources withdrawal factor in the basin.

title: The Attention Asymmetry Hypothesis: Retail Investors Avoid Bad News, and Post-Announcement Drift Pays the Price

detail.title: The Attention Asymmetry Hypothesis: Retail Investors Avoid Bad News, and Post-Announcement Drift Pays the Price

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known financial or personal conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study relied exclusively on publicly available data sources and did not involve human subjects, personal identifiable information, or experimental intervention requiring formal ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Post-earnings announcement drift is asymmetric: negative earnings surprises generate larger and more persistent drift than positive surprises of comparable magnitude. We propose and test the attention asymmetry hypothesis, which holds that this pattern reflects a systematic gap in how retail investors allocate attention across the two types of news. Using abnormal Google search volume (ASVI) as a direct measure of retail attention and a sample of 62,441 S&P 1500 firm-quarter observations from 2004 through 2022, we establish three results. First, ASVI in the five trading days before a negative earnings surprise averages-0.021 log units, compared with +0.068 for positive surprises of equivalent magnitude. The gap grows monotonically with surprise size, reaching 0.205 log units in the largest surprise quintile (t-statistic = 14.74). Second, 60-day post-announcement drift is 4.88% in absolute value for negative-surprise firms in the lowest attention quintile, compared with 1.64% for those in the highest attention quintile. The equivalent spread for positive surprises is 3.81% to 1.44%. Attention compresses negative drift substantially more than positive drift. Third, Fama-MacBeth regressions confirm that the interaction of NegSUE and ASVI enters with a coefficient of approximately-0.53, significant at the 1% level across all specifications. The findings are consistent with the disposition effect and self-attribution bias generating a pre-announcement gap in retail engagement that delays the market incorporation of bad earnings news. Hirshleifer, Lim, and Teoh (2009) show that extraneous competing announcements slow drift; we show that insufficient self-directed attention does the same, and that this insufficiency is specifically concentrated on the negative side.

title: Hybrid Credit Risk and Uncertainty Rating-Based AI Sociotechnical Expertocracy
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: Hybrid Credit Risk and Uncertainty Rating-Based AI Sociotechnical Expertocracy
detail.abstract: Widespread, precarious sovereign credit risk management and technoscientific rating expertise repeatedly precipitating and exacerbating financial and ”environmental, social, and governance” (ESG) crises remain taken for granted and virtually unaccountable. I problematize how professional, geometric-based ”debt sustainability analysis” (DSA) accounting ill-informs algorithmic/automated decision-making (ADM) fixed-income futurity financialization, embedding a (neoliberal) political economy of creditworthiness (PEC). Deconstruction/reconstruction of credit rating agency (CRA) and investor hybrid ”default risk/uncertainty” DSA techno-managerial modalities reveals synergistic sociotechnical rating methods/modeling digitalization promotes (unsustainable) ”business as usual.” Advancing sustainability management accounting through economic sociology, I analyze suspect ratings-assimilated market ADM/AI ”expertocracy” – knowledge-based expert rule – (re)validation of tenuous organizational conditions and professional affinities entrenches data and ESG imbalances. Technoscientific ratings constitute and reproduce a crisis-prone PEC ”inertia,” yet mutual (CRA/investor) mitigation effects impeding serious contestation and reform. Unpacking S&P, Moody’s, and Vanguard platforms, I study scores Passive/Active management facilitation in their operational contexts to better explain their AI/ADM-advanced analytical, organizational, and normative CRA correspondence. Financial AI-machine learning (ML) reinforces ratings (reflexive) professional performance. Enacting a misguided (disinflationary) PEC referential/data infrastructure stasis, consequently, AI-ML amplifies global (corporate) expertocracy, national democracy, and environmental asymmetries. Necessary for rebalanced alternatives, my scrutiny helps disturb seemingly ”self-systemic,” ”self-regulating” (neoliberal) capitalist PEC digitalization dominance.

title: Supervised Data Splitting for Image Data
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Supervised Data Splitting for Image Data
detail.abstract: Accurate image classification relies heavily on the quality of training and validation dataset splits, which directly influence a model's ability to reduce generalization error. While random sampling is widely used for the purpose of data splitting for model training purposes, it could produce non-representative subsets. Although several advanced data-splitting methods exist, most are designed for vector-based data and fail to account for the intricacies of image features. In this paper, we introduce Imalyke, a novel data-splitting method tailored for image data. Imalyke leverages feature extraction obtained via transfer learning and integrates them with Alyke, the state-of-the-art supervised data splitting method. We demonstrate with real-world image datasets that Imalyke produces representative and optimal dataset partitions, leading to improved model performance for image classification.

title: Sources, environmental risk assessment, and multi-factor spatial drivers of urban traffic congestion
affiliations: Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology and Kunming University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Sources, environmental risk assessment, and multi-factor spatial drivers of urban traffic congestion
detail.abstract: Urban traffic congestion’s environmental impacts are widely noted, but research on multi-factor source contributions and spatial drivers remains insufficient. This study integrates PCA/PMF, risk assessment, and a geographical detector in a mountainous city to decouple congestion sources, evaluate risks, and infer spatial drivers. Four sources are identified: structural supply-demand imbalance (35.02%, highest persistent risk), operational efficiency and behavior (23.05%), external disturbances (13.88%), and regulatory policies (28.05%). Distinct drivers: structural imbalance by GDP density (q=0.47) and vehicle ownership (q=0.42); operational efficiency by ITS coverage (q=0.48) and digital mobility penetration (q=0.41); regulatory policy by governance investment (q=0.48). All factor interactions amplify, notably governance investment ∩ digital mobility (q=0.864). We recommend zone-differentiated strategies based on source-specific spatial heterogeneity and driver combinations, offering a replicable diagnostic tool for mitigation and emission reduction.

title: Bitcoin Price Movements and Retail Crypto Adoption Interest Across Countries: The Role of Financial Development and Exchange Rate Volatility

detail.title: Bitcoin Price Movements and Retail Crypto Adoption Interest Across Countries: The Role of Financial Development and Exchange Rate Volatility
detail.abstract: This thesis examined whether retail crypto entry interest in G20 economies was systematically associated with Bitcoin price movements, and whether that association varied with two country level structural conditions: the depth of the domestic financial system and the volatility of the local currency. Prior crosscountry work had documented heterogeneous retail responses to Bitcoin rallies without probing the macro financial conditions that shaped them, and had not integrated Prospect Theory with Modern Portfolio Theory to explain such heterogeneity. The study addressed this gap through a quantitative, associational panel analysis of 19 G20 economies observed monthly from August 2015 through June 2022. Three hypotheses, each derived from the integrated theoretical framework, were then subjected to empirical testing. Lagged Bitcoin returns were positively and robustly associated with retail crypto application downloads. An asymmetry specification showed that both positive and negative return episodes were associated with higher downloads, consistent with an attention-based rather than a directional returnchasing pattern. Financial development was positively associated with responsiveness to Bitcoin returns, contrary to the opportunity cost prediction. Exchange rate volatility moderation was positive in direction but sensitive to the inference procedure. The thesis contributes cross country empirical evidence on the structural moderators of retail crypto entry, offers a reinterpretation of financial development as a proxy for access infrastructure, and refines the return chasing account of cryptocurrency adoption.

title: Multiscale and Polarized Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Inpainting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Multiscale and Polarized Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Inpainting
detail.abstract: Image inpainting aims to reconstruct missing pixels in images. Recently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) have achieved good performance in image inpainting. However, existing GANs-based methods still perform poorly on large damaged regions because they often require large amounts of training data and tend to lose detail information due to excessive dimensional compression in the generator. To address these problems, we propose an image inpainting method based on multiscale and polarized self-attention generative adversarial network, called MPA-GAN. Multiscale blocks are used to simultaneously learn the detailed information of low-level features and the rich semantic information of high-level features to improve the restoration of large damaged images. In addition, a polarized self-attention module is employed to alleviate information loss caused by dimensional compression, enabling better recovery of both small and large missing areas. Experiments are conducted on three commonly used image inpainting datasets: Paris StreetView, CelebA-HQ, and Places2. The results show the proposed methods achieved good performance on large-area image inpainting.

title: Beyond Structural Explanations: Causal Configurations of Authoritarian Regime Collapse during the Arab Spring

detail.title: Beyond Structural Explanations: Causal Configurations of Authoritarian Regime Collapse during the Arab Spring
detail.abstract: Why do comparable military defections and elite divisions sometimes produce regime collapse while identical conditions fail elsewhere? Conventional explanations falter by assuming uniform effects rather than context-dependent configurations. This article argues that breakdown arises from conjunctural combinations, transcending variable-centred approaches via Qualitative Comparative Analysis of eleven high-intensity protest cases from 2010-2014. Military insubordination, elite fragmentation, and the absence of external support prove necessary and jointly sufficient for collapse. Two equifinal pathways emerge: endogenous breakdown through domestic fragmentation without external support; and externally assisted collapse fuelled by foreign intervention. Structural factor such as youth unemployment and institutional weakness, however, do not achieve conventional necessity thresholds, acting as permissive enablers of mobilisation rather than determinants of outcomes. This set-theoretic test advances configurational methods, explaining divergent trajectories in similar cases while challenging monocausal and linear approaches.

title: Selective Few-Shot Test-Time Residual Correction for Frozen Forecast Generators
affiliations: Brawijaya University, Brawijaya University and Brawijaya University

detail.title: Selective Few-Shot Test-Time Residual Correction for Frozen Forecast Generators
detail.abstract: Time-series foundation models can provide strong zero-shot forecasts, but post-hoc correction from a few labeled target windows can be unreliable. We propose Few-Shot Test-Time Calibration (FS-TTC), where calibration denotes point-forecast residual correction rather than probabilistic or interval calibration. FS-TTC is a lightweight post-hoc selector for residual correction on top of frozen forecast generators. To reduce small-support overfitting, FS-TTC evaluates weighted interpolations between the zero-shot forecast and each correction candidate and retains the uncorrected zero-shot forecast unless a non-identity correction is stable across nested support-size checks. The backbone remains unchanged, and the selector uses only forecast outputs, support residuals, and optional predictive dispersion. On ten multivariate benchmarks covering 1769 variables and 30 dataset–seed pairs, FS-TTC selects active correction in 6 pairs and retains the zero-shot forecast in 24 pairs, improving mean relative scaled MAE by 1.39% without increasing MAE on any evaluated pair. Supplementary diagnostics further characterize when output-level residual correction is beneficial.

title: KPO-Market And Business Research on "Consumer's Attitude Towards the DIGITAL PAYMENTS"

detail.title: KPO-Market And Business Research on "Consumer's Attitude Towards the DIGITAL PAYMENTS"
detail.abstract:
This study examines consumer attitudes towards digital payment methods in India, focusing on the role of perceived usefulness and perceived security as key determinants of adoption behaviour. Using a quantitative cross-sectional research design, primary data were collected from 50 respondents through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. Descriptive statistical analysis including mean, median, mode, and standard deviation was applied to interpret the findings.
Results indicate that 82% of respondents actively use digital payment methods, with 39% reporting always using them. Paytm emerged as the dominant platform (73.2%), with UPI as the preferred payment method (68.3%). Speed (36.5%) and convenience (31.7%) were identified as the primary motivators for adoption, while technological complexity (29.3%) and security concerns (17.1%) remain notable barriers. A significant proportion of respondents (75.7%) expressed moderate to extreme concern about financial data security, with biometric authentication (39%) preferred as the most effective security enhancement.
The findings suggest that while digital payment adoption is growing rapidly, security infrastructure and user education must be strengthened to sustain long-term consumer trust. This study provides foundational insights into digital payment behaviour in an emerging economy context, with implications for platform developers and policymakers.

title: Battery degradation, operations, and charging in electric buses: a literature review
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universidad Autonoma de Yucatan, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tecnológico Nacional de México and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Battery degradation, operations, and charging in electric buses: a literature review
detail.abstract: Electric buses powered by lithiumion batteries are increasingly adopted as a strategy to decarbonize urban transportation, yet their large-scale implementation presents significant challenges related to energy consumption, battery degradation, and the planning of fleets and charging systems. This study examines the scientific literature on lithiumion battery electric buses through a combined bibliometric analysis and a conceptguided systematic review. A dataset of 1,194 articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (1992–2026) was compiled using a reproducible search strategy. The bibliometric analysis characterizes the evolution of the field, leading contributors, international collaboration networks, and emerging thematic clusters. Results reveal a 12.19% annual growth rate and highlight prevalent topics, including energy management, battery aging, charging strategies, and fleet scheduling. The review shows that battery degradation is still insufficiently integrated into planning models. The study proposes an integrative framework and outlines a research agenda emphasizing multiscale optimization, uncertainty modeling, and realworld validation.

detail.abstract:
The instruments that define macroeconomic monitoring — GDP, unemployment rates, price indices, the yield curve, and labor market confirmation indicators — each measure a specific subsystem of the economy with documented precision. None measure whether households across the income distribution can maintain operational viability and buffer adequacy under ordinary economic conditions. This exclusion is structural: a consequence of aggregate observational architecture that mathematically eliminates distributional heterogeneity, threshold proximity, and synchronization structure before any instrument observes the data.
This paper proposes the Propagation Chain Theory of Economic Indicators — a framework establishing that economic deterioration follows a documented chain from household financial stress through consumer spending contraction and business revenue decline to labor market confirmation. Each major economic indicator observes a different node in this chain. The household balance sheet — the chain’s origin — is currently unobserved by any systematic monitoring instrument.
The Household Viability Framework (HVF) formalizes household economic function as a conjunctive system of flow components supported by a reserve buffer. Below-threshold buffer conditions produce cascade vulnerability — nonlinear deterioration dynamics invisible to aggregate measures. Synchronized directional deterioration across income tiers constitutes a qualitatively distinct systemic signal consistent with broad-based resilience erosion.
The Household Economic Health Indicator (HEHI) is presented as one documented, replicable reference implementation of a household-side observation instrument. Applied across eleven US states over a 57-year dataset, the HEHI Momentum Indicator preceded each documented recession in the observed sample by eleven to fifteen months — consistent with the framework’s proposed propagation mechanism.
The paper’s primary contribution is methodological: a measurement-architecture theory for the systematic inclusion of household-side observation in macroeconomic monitoring, and a coordinate system for placing existing and future indicators within a documented propagation chain.

title: Green Marine Fuel Diffusion under Low-Carbon Policies: A System Dynamics Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai Institute of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Green Marine Fuel Diffusion under Low-Carbon Policies: A System Dynamics Analysis
detail.abstract: As decarbonization pressures intensify in shipping, the diffusion of green marine fuel technologies remains constrained by high costs, infrastructure dependence, and fuel supply uncertainty. This study develops a system dynamics model to examine how government subsidies and carbon pricing affect the diffusion of green marine fuels. The model integrates shipowners’ adoption decisions, shipbuilding learning, infrastructure development, fuel supply adjustment, and policy intervention. Results show that subsidies significantly accelerate market take-off and improve long-term diffusion. In single-stage scenarios, the green-fuel vessel share increases from about 63% under low subsidies to over 81% under high subsidies by 2050, while annual carbon emissions decrease by more than 12%. Two-stage simulations further indicate that policy effectiveness depends on both timing and sequencing: early support helps overcome initial barriers, whereas later adjustment shapes terminal market structure and emission outcomes. The findings highlight the need for staged policy design coordinated with infrastructure and fuel supply development.

title: Corporate Market Culture and Climate Performance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, The University of Manchester - Alliance Manchester Business School and The University of Manchester - Manchester Business School

detail.title: Corporate Market Culture and Climate Performance
detail.abstract: We examine whether corporate culture explains cross-sectional variation in firms' carbon performance, focusing specifically on the externally oriented market culture within the Competing Values Framework. Using textual analysis of 10-K filings for 16,564 U.S. firm-year observations, we find that firms with a stronger market-oriented culture, which emphasizes competition and responsiveness to external stakeholders, exhibit significantly lower carbon intensity. This association is economically meaningful and robust to multiple empirical tests, including a quasi-difference-in-differences design around CEO turnovers. Cross-sectional tests also show that the reported effect attenuates in settings where cultural transmission or external pressure is more limited, including in high labor mobility industries, and firms with concentrated customer bases. We also find a weaker effect in periods following climate regulation, when regulatory pressure may substitute for market-based cultural incentives.  We contribute to the literature by identifying corporate culture as an important but underexplored determinant of carbon performance and by showing that externally oriented cultural traits can align environmental outcomes with market incentives.

title: The Skill Content of AI: First-Personal Experience and Returns to Human Capital
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: The Skill Content of AI: First-Personal Experience and Returns to Human Capital
detail.abstract: AI has a structural limit: its training data contains no first-personal experience. Many exposure measures miss this — they track cognitive complexity but are largely silent on whether tasks require first-personal skill. We study optimal human capital investment in a model where humans and AI are symmetric learners, identical except in compute and data. Tasks combine distributional and first-personal skills, and are assigned to either humans or AI. Tasks with sufficient first-personal content remain permanently in the human domain, regardless of how cheap AI becomes. As AI cheapens, a Baumol channel raises the wage of first-personal skill, which overtakes ordinary cognitive skill if human-exclusive tasks are sufficiently first-personal-skill intensive. Optimal investment shifts toward first-personal skill; investment in distributional skill is non-monotone — falling as routine cognitive work moves to AI, then recovering.

title: A Prisoner's Dilemma in the coopetitive mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) system
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

detail.title: A Prisoner's Dilemma in the coopetitive mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) system
detail.abstract: This study develops a multi-leader–multi-follower game to model the interactions among a Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) platform, multiple transportation network companies (TNCs), mass transit (MT), and travelers in a bi-level framework. At the upper level, MaaS and TNCs simultaneously optimize their operational strategies and engage in the service capacity trading to maximize their profits, while at the lower level, heterogeneous travelers choose among available travel modes to maximize their utilities. The bi-level framework thus provides an analytical tool to characterize the coopetition between MaaS and TNCs in an aggregate mobility service market. We prove the existence of a Prisoner's Dilemma between MaaS and TNCs that prevents them from cooperating and leads to a suboptimal market outcome for both service operators and MaaS. To address such inefficiency, we propose a two-stage cooperative framework. In the first stage, MaaS and TNCs jointly optimize service design to maximize total profit, accounting for market equilibrium response. In the second stage, the profit generated from cooperation is distributed through a Nash bargaining process that determines the wholesale prices of service capacity. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this cooperative framework can induce a "win-win-win" situation, though the exclusive participation of large TNCs may disadvantage smaller operators and increase market fragmentation. To generate practical insights into MaaS, we further explore the market conditions under which MaaS fails to make a profit, and where TNCs adopt an "all-in" strategy, i.e., selling all their service capacities to MaaS.

title: Sequential planning of V2G-capable EV charging infrastructure under transportation–grid coupling and disruptions

detail.title: Sequential planning of V2G-capable EV charging infrastructure under transportation–grid coupling and disruptions
detail.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is becoming an important component of urban transportation systems because it affects route feasibility, charging delay, mobility coverage, and service continuity during disruptions. Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capability further links charging-infrastructure decisions to power-grid resilience. This paper develops a sequential planning framework for V2G-capable EV charging infrastructure in coupled transportation–grid systems under normal and disrupted conditions. The planner decides where, when, and what type of infrastructure to install over a multi-period horizon subject to budget, location, technology, and operational constraints. Each decision is evaluated through two interacting environments: a charging-constrained transportation environment that captures feasible EV routes, equilibrium flow redistribution, charging-service burden, and mobility coverage; and a distribution-grid environment that captures charging load, feeder stress, voltage-security burden, V2G dispatch, and unserved critical load. A dual-environment reinforcement learning approach is developed to learn staged expansion policies while retaining optimization-based transportation and grid response models. Analytical dominance and monotonicity rules reduce the action space. A reduced Austin, Texas case study demonstrates the framework using public-data-anchored calibration. The best balanced policy installs Fast/V2G hubs at Downtown and Airport, improving the integrated system objective by 13.0% relative to the existing-infrastructure baseline. Sensitivity analyses show that preferred infrastructure sequences depend on mobility-access, resilience, budget, and V2G-value assumptions. The results show that V2G-capable charging infrastructure should be planned as an emerging transportation technology whose value depends jointly on mobility access, charging-service quality, grid impacts, and disruption resilience.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a new territorial governance paradigm for Italy, termed “National Territorial Verticalization”, grounded in the contemporary reinterpretation of the historical transhumance system and its infrastructural corridors – the tratturi. Through a critical analysis of the failure of horizontal Italian regionalism and the persistent North-South territorial divide, the paper develops an institutional framework redesigning national governance around five north-south Strategic National Corridors. The proposal integrates spatial governance, interregional coordination, corridor-based development policies, infrastructure planning and place-based territorial governance. The framework includes a detailed institutional architecture, a multi-phase implementation roadmap and a preliminary cost-benefit analysis. The central thesis is that Italy possesses a deeply vertical geographical and historical vocation systematically ignored by horizontal regional policies.

title: Refuelling aircrafts: Operations planning for environmental sustainability
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Visakhapatnam and Indian Institute of Management Bodh Gaya

detail.title: Refuelling aircrafts: Operations planning for environmental sustainability
detail.abstract: Aircrafts refuelling is a critical ground activity at airports which has to be executed within tight turnaround times, particularly for transit flights. We argue that the amount of refuelling quantity (uplift quantity) is decided on the destination of the flight and the load factor, that is, number of passengers the airplane is carrying and the route it takes to reach the destination. The companies in oil and gas industry have to face a challenging task to ensure in-time refuelling to aircrafts and have to plan the most efficient way to refuel the aircrafts within the available time and other constraints, like, the availability of refuelling tanks. We develop mixed integer programming models . In order to ensure reduced carbon emissions in alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals, this paper attempts minimising the time to perform the task that involves the efficient allocation of refuelling tanks used for refuelling aircrafts.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of latency-sensitive Internet of Things (IoT) applications has brought serious computational challenges at the network edge. While most of the recent works use Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADDPG) for the computational offloading and resource allocation problems, these black-box AI models undergo long training times, incur high computational costs, and lack the adaptability in environments with high degree of non-stationarity. This paper aims to address the emerging ‘AI-fatigue’ in ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) networks by proposing a resource allocation mechanism based on Double-Sided Walrasian Auction and is solely deterministic and decentralized. Dynamic trading market allows us to model the collaborative Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) network to derive, for the first time, the exact KKT (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker) optimal bid strategies for IoT devices (bidders) and edge servers (sellers). An innovative discrete-time \emph{tâtonnement} price-adjustment procedure, combined with gradient clipping, is utilized to balance computational demand with available server capacity. The proposed model is validated by simulation with the real world dataset of Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC). The findings confirm the proposed model's mathematical framework for resource pricing optimization and market clearing. The proposed Walrasian mechanism has up to three orders of magnitude improvement in execution time. Additionally, it is the only model to demonstrate resource pricing optimization and market clearing along with the first and only bound on server energy and maximization of system social welfare propositions even in cases of high network load of 5000 devices. The proposed Walrasian mechanism demonstrates exceptional saturation and a high level of load capacity. Overall, the Walrasian mechanism demonstrates exceptional efficiency, reliability, and saturation management while illustrating an unparalleled reduction in the time needed for training neural networks.

title: Revisiting exchange rate predictability: Can machine learning with theoretical Filtering outperform canonical models?
affiliations: University of Central Florida and Mount Holyoke College - Department of Economics, University of Central Florida - College of Business Administration - Department of Economics

detail.title: Revisiting exchange rate predictability: Can machine learning with theoretical Filtering outperform canonical models?
detail.abstract: We revisit the exchange rate predictability puzzle by asking whether standard, widely used machine learning (ML) algorithms convincingly improve exchange rate forecasting. Using monthly data, we study US dollar to British pound as the baseline case (in both levels and monthly percent changes). We compare five ML methods -  random forests, neural networks, LASSO, gradient boosting, and linear support-vector classification- against canonical benchmarks (random walk and ARIMA) in a rolling one-step-ahead out-of-sample forecasting design. To mitigate sensitivity to stochastic estimation, we average forecasts across multiple seeds and assess performance using RMSE and Diebold-Mariano tests. We find that ML does not improve level forecasts and typically underperforms both benchmarks. For exchange rate changes, ML methods consistently outperform the random walk benchmark, but only neural networks - under a specific design - reliably beat ARIMA. We show that a unique theory-based UIP/PPP filtering approach improves accuracy for both ML and univariate methods, yet does not change the overall ranking. Extensive robust-ness checks across windows, currencies, frequencies, and tuning choices confirm that ML's advantages are limited and fragile relative to conventional univariate benchmarks.

title: The Role of Communication Skills in Auditing: Implications for Audit Quality, Fees, and Career Progression
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Haas School of Business, University of San Francisco,  and Drexel University

detail.title: The Role of Communication Skills in Auditing: Implications for Audit Quality, Fees, and Career Progression
detail.abstract: We leverage a unique dataset of employment profiles covering 86% of all employees at large U.S. public accounting firms to examine the relationship between auditors' communication skills and audit quality, audit fees, and auditors' career progression. We document that a higher share of employees with communication skills within an audit office is negatively associated with the number of restatements, including restatements related to complex accounting issues and missed internal control weaknesses (ICW), and positively associated with audit report timeliness and audit fees. The link between communication skills and audit quality is particularly strong for complex audit clients, where effective coordination and clear communication are crucial. We also find that female auditors' communication skills contribute more to audit quality and audit fees. Despite their clear benefits to overall audit quality, individual employees do not appear to gain personal career advantages (getting promoted or staying longer with the firm) from possessing communication skills unless they work in offices with high overall levels of communication.

detail.abstract: This paper examines delayed overseas income disclosure among new UK tax residents and proposes a Residency Tax Orientation Statement (RTOS) as an early guidance intervention within HM Revenue and Customs' (HMRC) Government Gateway digital services. It identifies a recurring compliance pattern in which some individuals entering the UK tax system through Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) employment treat employer withholding as if it settles their full tax obligations. As a result, overseas income, including rental receipts, business profit distributions, foreign investment returns, and overseas pension income, may remain undeclared for several tax years. In some cases, HMRC detects such non-compliance only after a substantial delay, by which point retrospective assessment, interest charges, and penalties may be difficult to avoid. The proposed RTOS would address this information gap through a brief yes-or-no orientation check presented at an early administrative touchpoint, directing users to relevant guidance without creating tax liability, requiring asset disclosure, or triggering enforcement action. Drawing on behavioural tax compliance theory, comparative tax administration, and published HMRC administrative data, the paper argues that a low-cost, well-timed intervention within existing digital infrastructure may help reduce delayed disclosure, improve taxpayers' understanding of worldwide income obligations, and lower the volume of multi-year compliance investigations. More broadly, the paper shows how a preventative compliance approach may be incorporated into existing UK administrative arrangements.

title: U.S. Monetary Tightening and External Debt Sustainability in Emerging Markets

detail.title: U.S. Monetary Tightening and External Debt Sustainability in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: This paper documents the dynamic relationship between U.S. monetary policy tightening and external debt sustainability in a panel of 31 emerging and frontier economies over the period 2004-2024. Using fixed-effects regressions and local projections, we find that a 100-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate is associated with a gradual, persistent rise in the external debt-to-GNI ratio of approximately 2.4 percentage points after four years. The association is strongest in the Middle East and North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa, while Latin America also shows a statistically significant positive coefficient. An interaction local-projection framework reveals significantly smaller debt accumulation for countries with larger foreign-exchange reserves, with the buffering effect becoming statistically significant at the three-and four-year horizons. The results are descriptive; an attempt to use high-frequency monetary surprises as an instrument failed due to weak first-stage relationships. The evidence is robust to alternative specifications and highlights the potential value of reserve stocks in insulating emerging markets from global financial cycle swings.

title: An Intelligent Framework for Data Center Cooling Optimization Using ANN–GA and TES to Reduce Energy Consumption and Carbon Footprint
affiliations: Sharif University of Technology, Sharif University of Technology and Sharif University of Technology

detail.title: An Intelligent Framework for Data Center Cooling Optimization Using ANN–GA and TES to Reduce Energy Consumption and Carbon Footprint
detail.abstract: Developing a sustainable cooling solution that can simultaneously reduce operating costs and the carbon footprint is both critical and necessary for modern data centers. This paper proposes an integrated, storage-aware optimization framework that combines a high-accuracy Artificial Neural Network (ANN) predictor with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimizer and a chilled-water Thermal Energy Storage (TES) system. The ANN is trained using data from a real facility to predict rack inlet temperatures and fan factors, enabling rapid assessment of candidate control actions without the computational burden of CFD-based evaluation. Building on these predictions, the GA jointly optimizes supply-air temperature, fan operation, and TES charging/discharging over a 24-hour horizon while strictly enforcing thermal reliability constraints, allowing safe operation at higher inlet temperatures (up to 30 °C). The optimization explicitly incorporates time-varying electricity price, outdoor ambient temperature, hourly carbon-intensity signals, and dynamic rack heat-load profiles. Results indicate that integrating TES into the core optimization loop, rather than treating it as a backup, can reduce cooling-related energy cost by up to 21% while maintaining the required thermal limits, and can also reduce carbon emissions by up to 9% under favorable operating conditions. In fact, carbon-oriented optimization shows weaker gains overall, likely due to the complex interaction between carbon-intensity patterns and ambient-temperature-driven chiller efficiency, as well as the highly non-linear search space that can increase sensitivity to local optima; in some free-cooling-dominant periods, TES cycling may provide limited benefit. Overall, the proposed framework brings predictive intelligence and thermal physics into a cohesive control strategy, offering a practical route toward “storage-aware” operation and providing quantitative guidance for data center operators seeking low-cost, low-carbon cooling upgrades.

detail.abstract: Governance has very often been pointed at the developments approaches as the main cause of development delays and political instability in African countries such as Mali. The question of security, which is added to the chapel of the grievances expressed by the populations towards their governments, continues to arouse the interest of many research works that have such relevance. What role can good governance play in the concern for the construction of security and peace, measures of stability and development in the Allies in a context of geopolitical uncertainty? The lack of governance as a factor in the fragility of the State aggravated by the geopolitical issues also increases the level of insecurity in the country with its evident repercussions in the Sahel. The study examines the mechanisms by which state fragility feeds regional insecurity, analyses attempt at institutional refoundation and formulates recommendations for post-crisis reconstruction.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Finance Value Pyramid-a three-level conceptual framework that classifies finance function activities according to their strategic value contribution: Data Work (Level 1), Analytical Work (Level 2), and Narrative Work (Level 3). Unlike prior financetransformation research that focuses primarily on technical efficiency, this article argues that the emergence of generative AI and large language models (LLMs) accentuates a pre-existing value asymmetry: LLMs substantially automate Data Work (Eloundou et al., 2024), augment Analytical Work while preserving human interpretive judgment (Yigitbasioglu et al., 2023), and leave Narrative Work-the highest-value domain-as the most resilient human advantage. Through critical synthesis of three literature domains-decision usefulness theory (Beaver, 1968; IASB, 2018), the evolution of management accounting toward business partnering (Lambert & Sponem, 2012; Goretzki & Messner, 2019), and AI impact on cognitive work (Frey & Osborne, 2017; Eloundou et al., 2024)-the framework derives each pyramid level analytically from decision-usefulness criteria and proposes an extension of that theory to incorporate narrative translation as an explicit dimension of actual usefulness. Three conceptual propositions are advanced together with a falsifiable empirical research agenda.

title: Japan's Narrow Defense Export Path Structural Constraints, Alliance Positioning, and the Limits of Tokyo's Arms Export Liberalization

detail.title: Japan's Narrow Defense Export Path Structural Constraints, Alliance Positioning, and the Limits of Tokyo's Arms Export Liberalization

keywords: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Japan's Narrow Defense Export Path

detail.abstract: Japan is entering the global arms market through a narrow door. After decades of postwar restraint, Tokyo's revision to the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technologypermitting lethal weapons transfers to allied countries not in active conflict-marks a significant shift in defense industrial policy. This paper argues that easing export restrictions does not, in itself, make Japan a competitive arms exporter. Its entry into global markets is structurally constrained by limited production capacity, high per-unit costs, the absence of combat-proven systems, and a regulatory framework that remains more restrictive than South Korea's export-oriented model or China's state-backed mass production approach. Rather than pursuing volume-based competition, Japan's viable path lies in strategic positioning within high-end, technologically sophisticated niches-aerospace systems, submarine technology, and integrated sensor networks-that leverage its advanced engineering capabilities and alliance interoperability. The paper examines two forward scenarios: GCAP technology leadership in sixth-generation air combat, and a niche maritime defense market driven by escalating South China Sea tensions. It concludes that Japan's defense export opening is unlikely to transform it into a volume competitor; its strategic significance lies instead in the emergence of a selective, alliance-centred model built around advanced technology, interoperability, and trusted partnerships.

title: Living Well — From Stoicism to Modern Psychology

detail.title: Living Well — From Stoicism to Modern Psychology
detail.abstract: A cross-temporal investigation of what it means to live well, tracing the question from Stoic philosophy through contemporary positive psychology. The paper examines how ancient frameworks for the good life — virtue ethics, acceptance of fate, the distinction between what we control and what we cannot — resurface in modern therapeutic and self-help contexts, often stripped of their philosophical depth. It asks whether psychology has answered the question the Stoics posed, or merely repackaged it.

title: How Concentrated Are Indian Equity Indices? A Coverage-Aware Framework for Measuring HHI, Top-N, Effective-N, and Sector Concentration

detail.title: How Concentrated Are Indian Equity Indices? A Coverage-Aware Framework for Measuring HHI, Top-N, Effective-N, and Sector Concentration

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a public-source, coverage-aware framework for measuring concentration in major Indian equity indices. The study uses current constituent and sector weightage data for Nifty 50, Nifty Next 50, Nifty 100, Nifty 500, Nifty Bank, Nifty IT, Nifty FMCG, Nifty Auto, and BSE Sensex. The central methodological contribution is not merely the calculation of Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI), Top-N concentration ratios, effective number of stocks, Shannon entropy, Theil concentration, and sector HHI; it is the explicit separation of full-constituent snapshots from top-10-only snapshots and sector-level snapshots. This distinction is essential because several official public factsheets disclose only the ten largest constituent weights while providing complete sector breakdowns.

The current-snapshot evidence indicates that nominal index breadth can materially overstate economic diversification. Broad indices display lower concentration than sectoral indices, but concentration remains economically meaningful: the Nifty 50 top ten constituents account for 53.68% of index weight, while the BSE Sensex top ten account for 65.28% using full-constituent BSE weightage data. Sectoral indices are substantially more concentrated, with Nifty IT, Nifty FMCG, Nifty Auto, and Nifty Bank displaying top-10 weights near or above 86%.

The paper contributes a reproducible data structure and research workflow that can be extended to historical snapshots, risk-linkage tests, and policy analysis under the SEBI Significant Indices framework. The findings are best interpreted as current-snapshot evidence and a transparent foundation for future concentration-drift analysis rather than as a final causal claim about index risk.

title: The Trilogy of One: An Integrated Statutory and Operational Playbook for the Pennsylvania Cannabis Sovereignty Framework

detail.abstract: This paper unifies three operational components of the Keystone framework — statutory text, implementation playbook, and execution timeline — into a single integrated reference document for legislative and administrative actors. The "Trilogy of One" structure derives from a documented institutional failure mode: statutory drafting, regulatory implementation, and operational stand-up are typically treated as sequential phases handled by different institutional actors (legislative counsel, regulatory agency staff, program implementers), producing implementation gaps that delay revenue generation by 12 to 36 months relative to the statutory enactment date. The Trilogy collapses these phases into a single document addressed to all three audiences simultaneously. It contains: (1) the core statutory text mapping to Senate Bill 420 and Senate Bill 49, with cross-references to the Omnibus Amendment (SSRN ID 6652358); (2) the operational playbook covering Department of Revenue, Department of Health, and Department of Agriculture coordination requirements, including Wholesale Portal Protocol implementation sequencing; and (3) the execution timeline targeting first revenue within 18 months of enactment. The paper is designed to be cited alongside the Keystone Mandate (SSRN ID 6507161) and the Keystone Doctrine (SSRN ID 6507160) as the operational complement to those foundational documents.

title: The Keystone Completion: Defining the End-State and Success Criteria for Pennsylvania's Cannabis Sovereignty Framework

detail.title: The Keystone Completion: Defining the End-State and Success Criteria for Pennsylvania's Cannabis Sovereignty Framework
detail.abstract: This paper specifies the success criteria, terminal-state metrics, and completion conditions for the Keystone reform framework. Where the Keystone Mandate (SSRN ID 6507161) establishes the legislative entry conditions and the Keystone Doctrine (SSRN ID 6507160) establishes the constitutional foundation, this paper defines what "completion" looks like as a measurable end-state — a deliberate response to a recurring failure mode in policy architecture, in which reform frameworks operate indefinitely without an articulated success threshold and therefore cannot be evaluated against their own stated goals. The Completion framework specifies fiscal completion criteria (target General Fund contribution, target Municipal Dividend distribution, terminal border-bleed reduction below a defined threshold), regulatory completion criteria (full operational capacity at Wholesale Portal level under Protocols 30.1–30.5, full Green Firewall compliance against synthetic cannabinoid penetration), and constitutional completion criteria (successful defense against any federal preemption challenge under Murphy v. NCAA and Printz v. United States). The Completion framework is designed to provide both legislative architects and oversight bodies with a clear, testable, and time-bounded terminal state, enabling subsequent legislatures to determine whether the framework has succeeded, requires extension, or warrants sunset.

title: China's Export Overcapacity and the Escalating US-China Trade Tensions: Implications for Global Trade Order (2023-2025)

detail.title: China's Export Overcapacity and the Escalating US-China Trade Tensions: Implications for Global Trade Order (2023-2025)
detail.abstract: Persistent industrial overcapacity in China-most visibly in steel, electric vehicles, solar photovoltaic panels, and electronics-has contributed to bilateral trade tensions with the United States and raised questions about the stability of the multilateral trading system. This paper examines the sectoral dimensions of this overcapacity, traces the trajectory of US policy responses, and assesses broader systemic implications for the period 2023-2025. The study employs a qualitative analytical review of secondary sources drawn from the International Energy Agency, World Bank, International Monetary Fund, World Trade Organization, and related institutions; it does not present original econometric findings. The analysis finds that Chinese manufacturing output in the examined sectors appears to substantially exceed domestic demand, while US countermeasures-including the CHIPS and Science Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the tariff escalations of 2025-raise questions of consistency with WTO rules. The paper concludes that current trajectories are consistent with a more fragmented and politically managed trade environment, with implications for supply chain governance, development strategy, and multilateral institutions.

title: Concept Migration, Complexity, and the Scientific Status of Economics: From Formalism to Evolving Systems

detail.title: Concept Migration, Complexity, and the Scientific Status of Economics: From Formalism to Evolving Systems

declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: This paper revisits the long-standing question of whether economics qualifies as a science by reframing it through the lens of concept migration and complexity. Building on Kenneth E. Boulding’s systems-oriented perspective and contrasting it with the formalist program associated with Paul Samuelson, the paper argues that the scientific status of economics depends not on its mathematical sophistication per se, but on the ontological fit between its methods and the evolving, adaptive nature of its subject matter. The paper identifies four camps in this debate: those who align economics with the formal rigor of physics; those who situate it among the evolutionary and 1 ecological sciences; those who seek a synthesis through complexity theory; and those who argue that economics fundamentally misspecifies its relationships by ignoring the role of energy as the primary productive force. Empirical illustrations and a formal appendix demonstrate how equilibrium relationships break down under shocks and interaction effects. The paper also considers the implications of rapid technological change—including artificial intelligence—for a discipline that once treated technology as a fixed parameter. Together, these threads point toward a conception of economics as an evolving system science, enriched but also challenged by interdisciplinary concept migration and the persistent growth of knowledge.

title: The Invisible Tax on India's Plate: Estimating the Macroeconomic Cost of Food Adulteration Through a Three-Channel Framework

detail.title: The Invisible Tax on India's Plate: Estimating the Macroeconomic Cost of Food Adulteration Through a Three-Channel Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. No personal or financial relationships with any person or organisation influenced this study.

detail.abstract:
Background: Food adulteration in India represents a systemic market failure with economic consequences extending far beyond public health. In FY 2023–24, FSSAI testing revealed that 22% of over 1.5 lakh food samples were non-conforming. Despite this scale, a systematic macroeconomic quantification of the aggregate annual cost to the Indian economy remains absent. This research gap prevents food safety enforcement from being advocated in the fiscal language required for budgetary prioritization.

Methods: This paper introduces the Three-Channel Cost Estimation (3-CCE) framework to decompose the macroeconomic impact into three distinct channels:

  1. Consumer welfare loss from nutritional fraud.

  2. Healthcare expenditure burden linked to adulteration-related illness.

  3. Foregone export revenue due to safety non-compliance.

The study utilizes official government datasets, including the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023–24 (MoSPI), National Health Accounts, and APEDA/DGFT export statistics. The framework adopts conservative assumptions, reporting results in lower-to-upper-bound ranges to ensure fiscal credibility.

Results: The aggregate annual economic cost of food adulteration in India is estimated at ₹1.45 to ₹2.23 lakh crore, representing 0.45% to 0.69% of India’s nominal GDP (FY 2024–25). Consumer welfare loss is the primary driver, accounting for roughly 79% of the total cost. Crucially, the analysis reveals that food adulteration acts as a regressive implicit tax: the proportional burden is 2.5 times higher for rural bottom-decile households than for urban top-decile households. Finally, benefit-cost analysis indicates that enforcement investment yields a conservative ratio of 3.65:1.

Conclusion: Food adulteration imposes a measurable economic cost that exceeds India's Union Budget health allocation by a factor of 1.6. These findings suggest that food safety enforcement should be reclassified from "regulatory overhead" to "productive economic infrastructure." The paper establishes a quantitative foundation for urgent fiscal intervention in food safety systems.

title: Israeli Occupation Detentions in Palestine: International Law and Human Rights Perspectives اعتقالات الاحتلال في فلسطين: بين القانون الدولي وحقوق الإنسان

detail.abstract: In recent weeks, the Palestinian territories have witnessed a notable escalation in arrest operations carried out by Israeli forces, including the issuance of more than 600 administrative detention orders within only two weeks. The Israeli occupation relies on the system of administrative detention, which permits detention without formal charges or public trial, based on a secret file that neither the detainee nor their lawyer is allowed to access, with the possibility of indefinite renewal. This article examines this policy in light of international standards, particularly Article 9 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which prohibits arbitrary detention. It also documents violations related to the right to liberty and personal security, the right to a fair trial, freedom from torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, and the right to communicate with family and counsel. The article concludes that prolonged administrative detention and cruel treatment may amount to the infliction of serious bodily or mental harm within a systematic pattern.

title: District Impact Addendum: The Geographic Distribution of Pennsylvania's Cannabis Opportunity Cost — A District-Level Forfeiture Analysis

detail.title: District Impact Addendum: The Geographic Distribution of Pennsylvania's Cannabis Opportunity Cost — A District-Level Forfeiture Analysis

detail.abstract: This Addendum disaggregates the Commonwealth-level cannabis "border bleed" estimate (approximately $18 million per month in capital flight to neighboring states) to the level of individual Pennsylvania Senate and House districts. Using a combination of cross-state retail sales data, license-plate survey methodologies adapted from border-state dispensary studies, and population-weighted demand modeling, the Addendum produces per-district forfeiture estimates demonstrating substantial geographic heterogeneity: high-bleed districts on the Maryland, New Jersey, New York, and Ohio borders register monthly forfeiture rates that produce documented 69-day district forfeitures of $828,000 in Senate District 29 (Argall) and Senate District 49 (Laughlin), while interior districts such as House District 60 (Major) register lower but still material 69-day forfeitures of approximately $204,000. The paper computes district-specific 69-day, 180-day, and 365-day cumulative forfeiture totals and presents them as the "Inaction Tax" — a quantification of the opportunity cost imposed on each district by continued legislative deadlock. The Addendum is designed for use by individual legislators in district-specific constituent communications and for the construction of district-by-district coalition-building strategy, complementing the qualitative coalition mapping in the Keystone Policy Prism volumes.

detail.abstract:
This paper advances a structural reinterpretation of the phrase “living Constitution” by reframing the United States Constitution not as an infinitely mutable political instrument, but as a bounded adaptive governance architecture designed to preserve institutional continuity, representative legitimacy, and constitutional survivability across changing historical conditions. Contemporary constitutional discourse frequently collapses distinctions between constitutional interpretation, amendment, policy evolution, institutional adaptation, and transient civic preference, producing conceptual instability regarding the nature of constitutional continuity itself. In response, this paper introduces the framework of Adaptive Constitutional Continuity (ACC): the capacity of a constitutional system to preserve procedural identity, operational coherence, and legitimacy across evolving technological, demographic, communicative, and political environments through constrained structural adaptation without dissolving constitutional continuity.

The paper argues that the enduring character of the American constitutional system emerges not from unrestricted interpretive elasticity, but from continuity-preserving mechanisms embedded throughout the constitutional architecture itself. Article V amendment procedures, federalism, bicameralism, jurisdictional segmentation, representative filtration, separation of powers, and temporal sequencing collectively function as constitutional stabilization mechanisms permitting adaptation while preserving systemic coherence across time. Under this framework, the Constitution remains “living” because it continuously processes changing civic conditions through bounded institutional translation rather than through unconstrained political synchronization.

To formalize this claim, the paper integrates constitutional systems theory with signal-processing architecture developed throughout the companion framework The First Amendment as Signal Architecture: Jurisdiction, Translation, and the Limits of Scale (2026). Through Figures 1–4, the paper models the constitutional sequence through which decentralized civic expression becomes attributable signal, undergoes representative and jurisdictional translation, and ultimately stabilizes into lawful authority formation within distributed constitutional structures. The analysis further argues that constitutional survivability depends not solely upon preserving institutional legality in the abstract, but also upon maintaining sufficient civic interpretability such that representative legitimacy, procedural coherence, and constitutional comprehension remain intelligible under conditions of increasing communicative scale.

The paper additionally introduces several interrelated doctrinal concepts—including the Adaptive Equilibrium Principle, Constitutional Survivability Boundary, Input Integrity as Constitutional Dependency, and the Executive as a Constitutional Coherence Node—to explain how constitutional systems preserve operational continuity under conditions of amplification pressure, institutional strain, and evolving informational environments. Historical constitutional development, including the Bill of Rights, Reconstruction Amendments, direct election of senators, and voting-rights expansion, is reinterpreted not as evidence of constitutional replacement, but as examples of continuity-preserving structural recalibration within the broader constitutional order.

Ultimately, this paper argues that the Constitution survives not because it remains static, nor because it continuously synchronizes with transient political pressure, but because it possesses lawful mechanisms capable of integrating evolving civic conditions while preserving the structural architecture necessary for long-horizon constitutional continuity. The “living” character of the Constitution therefore resides not in limitless interpretive mutability, but in adaptive constitutional continuity: the enduring capacity of the constitutional order to govern across changing historical conditions without surrendering the procedural foundations through which the Republic itself remains possible.

title: The Invisible Segment of the Night Market: Predicting the Opening Gap Based on Post-Settlement Distortions

detail.title: The Invisible Segment of the Night Market: Predicting the Opening Gap Based on Post-Settlement Distortions
detail.abstract:
The present study develops an advanced analytical framework for predicting opening gaps in global futures markets using a heterogeneous sample of 60 contracts spanning stock indices, commodities, Forex, cryptocurrencies, and government bonds. Two predictive architectures with three variables per model are evaluated and compared. First, the KaC model predicts the total displacement from the official Settle Price to the next market open. Second, the MK model independently decomposes the overnight return into two segments: the post-settle movement (from the official settle to the actual market close) and the opening gap itself. Results show that the independent MK model delivers risk-adjusted returns approximately three times higher than the joint KaC approach. Within this structure, the MBI indicator, a proprietary OHLC-based market pressure metric calculated using the settle price, emerges as the strongest predictor of the post-settle segment, while the post-settle price evolution itself provides the best predictive power for the opening gap.

The study concludes with a realistic operational implementation of the MK model, incorporating a detailed cost structure including round-trip commissions, exchange fees, opening and closing spreads, and slippage. To validate the robustness of the results, the models are tested using multiple In-Sample and Out-of-Sample configurations under three increasingly restrictive scenarios, as well as dynamic Walk-Forward and Robust Walk-Forward protocols. The analysis demonstrates that the predictive anomaly remains persistent across different market regimes and validation structures.

Finally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted by doubling all transaction costs to simulate adverse liquidity conditions and stressed execution environments. Although profitability naturally declines under these extreme assumptions, the model maintains relatively stable equity structures and remains close to break-even or positive in several scenarios, particularly after applying a quantitative filtering process based on Sharpe Ratio × R² selection criteria. These findings suggest that the post-settle segment and opening gap contain persistent and exploitable microstructural inefficiencies, provided that implementation is carried out through dynamic asset, direction, and temporal filtering under realistic trading conditions.

title: Predicting and Explaining Variation in U.S. Healthcare Costs Using Patient and Hospital-Level Data

detail.title: Predicting and Explaining Variation in U.S. Healthcare Costs Using Patient and Hospital-Level Data
detail.abstract: Healthcare cost variation remains one of the most significant challenges in the United States healthcare system. Despite substantial national healthcare expenditures, large differences persist in spending across patients, conditions, and healthcare providers. Understanding the factors that drive these variations is essential for improving efficiency, reducing unnecessary costs, and informing evidence-based healthcare policy. This study examines healthcare cost variation using a multi-level analytical framework that integrates patient-level data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) and hospitallevel data from Medicare inpatient claims. Predictive models were developed to estimate total healthcare expenditures at the patient level and average Medicare payments at the hospital level. The models evaluated include Linear Regression and Random Forest algorithms, which allow for both interpretability and the ability to capture complex relationships within the data. Model performance was assessed using standard regression metrics, including the coefficient of determination (R²), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), consistent with established approaches in healthcare analytics (Rajkomar et al., 2019; Obermeyer & Emanuel, 2016). The results demonstrate that healthcare costs can be predicted with high accuracy using demographic, clinical, and institutional variables. Chronic disease status, insurance coverage, and age were identified as key drivers of patient-level expenditures, while Diagnosis-Related Group (DRG) classification and discharge volume were significant predictors of hospital-level payment variation. The findings also reveal substantial inefficiencies in healthcare pricing, including large discrepancies between submitted hospital charges and Medicare payments. By integrating patientlevel and hospital-level analyses, this study provides a comprehensive understanding of healthcare cost drivers and demonstrates the value of predictive analytics in supporting cost containment strategies and healthcare policy decision-making.

title: The Impact of UPI on Consumer Spending Behavior and Financial Inclusion in India

detail.title: The Impact of UPI on Consumer Spending Behavior and Financial Inclusion in India
detail.abstract:
This dissertation examines the transformative impact of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) on India's financial ecosystem, focusing on the intersection of digital transformation, financial inclusion, and consumer spending behavior. Utilizing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and multi-dimensional segmentation, the research analyzes how UPI’s frictionless architecture influences diverse user cohorts. As of October 2025, UPI processed 20.7 billion transactions (₹27.28 lakh crore), commanding 85% of digital transaction volume. While this growth has significantly expanded formal financial access for micro-enterprises and unbanked populations, it has simultaneously introduced unintended behavioral shifts and systemic risks.
Empirical findings reveal sharp demographic disparities: 82% of Gen Z users report increased expenditure compared to 41% of seniors, while "power users" are 2.3 times more likely to exceed budgets. TAM analysis attributes these patterns to differential construct profiles, specifically hedonic motivation in younger segments and habit-mediated budget overruns in high-frequency users. Conversely, lower computer self-efficacy and higher anxiety correlate with increased fraud vulnerability among older and less-educated demographics—a critical concern given the 85% rise in UPI fraud (FY23-24) and losses exceeding ₹1,000 crore.

This study attempts to estimate the interactive effects on expenditures of the designation as a specially authorized city and merger, i.e. the interaction of economies of scope and scale. The findings of this research are summarized as follows. title: From Resistive Load to Regulated Flexibility: Economic and Policy-Constrained Performance of AI-Based Mining-Heating Systems

detail.title: From Resistive Load to Regulated Flexibility: Economic and Policy-Constrained Performance of AI-Based Mining-Heating Systems
detail.abstract: In terms of thermodynamics, proof-of-work blockchain mining is comparable to an electric resistive load whose electrical input is nearly completely dissipated as low-grade heat. This characteristic makes it possible to create mining-heating setups that serve two purposes: space heating and cryptographic computing. Nevertheless, rather than relying just on gross power use, the circumstances of the marginal grid, market exposure, and enforceable operational limits determine the environment and economic performance of such systems. In this study, mining-heating systems with AI are evaluated under certain legislative and economic constraints. A Bitmain Antminer S21 Pro (3.51 kW, 234 TH/s) is simulated using physics spanning realistic room volumes (60-340 m³) in a European comfort zone of 20-23 °C. The same thermal and economic assumptions are used to benchmark four control strategies: traditional electric resistance heating, hybrid modulation, reinforcement learning (Q-learning), and bang-bang. Price-aligned operation, marginal emissions conditions, and other governance-relevant situations are evaluated in addition to operational profit and comfort criteria. Bang-bang control yielded the largest comfort-valid profit under baseline deterministic settings (€108.41 at 160 m³), reinforcement learning (€103.73), hybrid modulation (€100.24), and electric resistance heating (-€116.77 at 60 m³). In its best comfort-valid scenario, reinforcement learning maintained 99.94 % time-in-band comfort and reduced duty to 95.69 % while achieving almost maximum profit. While bang-bang control generated the greatest best-case comfort-valid profit, hybrid control obtained the maximum comfort-feasible share over the entire simulated scenario set. Building-physics characteristics had lower secondary impacts, while network hashrate (-3.124 % profit per +1 % input), power price (-2.271 %), Bitcoin price (+2.115 %), and block reward (+2.115 %) dominated economic viability, according to the local elasticity analysis. Emissions results are conditional: mining-heated only lowers net system emissions when it replaces fossil fuel-based heating and is time-aligned with low-carbon or excess renewable power. The findings demonstrate that AI-controlled mining-heating systems may operate as programmable electric loads with potential flexibility value, but their feasibility is dependent on market alignment, marginal system conditions, and enforceable governance constraints.
